articles.title: Does Taguig have ghost flood control projects? The conflicting claims of Dizon and Lacson
articles.summary: Senator Ping Lacson disputes Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon’s statement, saying it contradicted site inspection reports prepared by DPWH personnel

blocks.text: Senator Ping Lacson disputes Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon’s statement, saying it contradicted site inspection reports prepared by DPWH personnel

items: Senator Panfilo Lacson claims to have identified at least 32 anomalous flood control projects in Taguig City, including two he labels as ghost projects.

Senator Alan Peter Cayetano disputes these claims, stating that the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) found no ghost projects in Taguig, although they confirmed 10 ghost projects nationwide.
Lacson maintains his position, citing evidence of irregularities and ongoing investigations, while highlighting the professional ties between Cayetano and DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – Are there really ghost flood control projects in Taguig City, the political bailiwick of the Cayetanos?
Senator Panfilo “Ping” Lacson has claimed that his team identified at least 32 allegedly anomalous flood control projects in Taguig City. At least two, according to Lacson, are ghost projects.
Senator Alan Peter Cayetano, however, has disputed allegations of ghost projects in the city.

During the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) budget hearing on Friday, September 25, Cayetano directly asked Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon whether the agency had found any ghost projects in Taguig.
“Ilan na ang conclusive na ghost project across the nation,” Cayetano asked. (How many ghost projects across the country have been conclusively identified?)
Dizon said there are 10 confirmed ghost projects so far.
“Are there any ghost projects in Taguig?” Cayetano followed up.
“Wala po. Sa aming imbestigasyon, wala po,” Dizon replied. (None. In our investigation, there’s none.)
Lacson disputed Dizon’s statement, saying it contradicted site inspection reports prepared by DPWH personnel.

“Poor DPWH Site Inspection Engineers. Their boss, Sec. Vince Dizon directly contradicted their own site inspection reports in Taguig, specifically submitted by personnel from the department’s Bureau of Quality and Safety and Bureau of Maintenance,” Lacson said in a social media post on Saturday, September 26.
Lacson has cited DPWH records involving a project supposedly located in Taguig but whose geotagged site photos reportedly showed coordinates in Leyte, around 600 kilometers away.
Lacson said Dizon called him after the Senate hearing and was “apologetic,” telling him that it appeared he had been “set up.”

For Lacson, it seems like that’s not the case. The senator sent a video to Dizon, an excerpt of the hearing when Dizon made the blanket denial that there’s no ghost flood control project in Taguig City.
Dizon, on Monday, September 28, clarified that there are 10 confirmed ghost flood control projects in the country so far but none is located in Taguig City.
Dizon also clarified that the investigation into the flood control projects in Taguig is still on-going.
Lacson has stood by his findings, saying he does not make allegations without “receipts” or proof.
In July, Lacson submitted evidence on alleged irregularities involving flood control projects in Taguig to the Office of the Ombudsman for review.
The professional ties between Dizon and Cayetano date back to 2013. Dizon served as a consultant to then-Senate majority ;eader Cayetano from 2013 to 2016, Dizon’s resumé shows.
Dizon later became president and CEO of the Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA).
During his time at the BCDA, Dizon was involved in preparations for the 2019 Southeast Asian (SEA) Games, while Cayetano chaired the Philippine SEA Games Organizing Committee.

blocks.caption: How Cayetano, Dizon got ‘cleared’ in 2019 SEA Games controversy

blocks.text: The SEA Games later drew scrutiny over the construction of its controversial cauldron.
In 2026, the National Bureau of Investigation started an investigation again into the alleged anomalies surrounding SEA games. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in Nations League match overshadowed by political controversy
articles.summary: Ireland easily beat Israel in a Nations League fixture that 24 hours earlier appeared in doubt. One Irish player pulled out of the match to express his opposition to Israel's actions in the Gaza…

image.caption: Members of the Irish team bowed their heads during playing of the Israeli national anthemImage: Inpho Photography/IMAGO

blocks.text: The Irish team bowed their heads during playing of the Israeli national anthem on Sunday night and they declined to shake hands with their opponents, a gesture that is customary before international fixtures.

Ireland played the match wearing black armbands in memory of those killed in Israel's military operation in the Gaza Strip, and just 24 hours earlier it was unclear whether the match would go ahead at all.
'Significant majority' vote to play
On Saturday, the players voted in favor of playing what was technically a home match for Israel in Debrecen, Hungary, despite widespread opposition to their participation among the Irish public.

David Courell, the chief executive of the Irish FA (FAI), told a press conference that had been delayed for several hours while players and coaches met to discuss the issue, that a significant majority of the squad had voted to play.
"Based on that, the association took ⁠the decision on behalf of Irish ​football that this fixture would continue, as we have always intended to fulfil the fixtures," he said.
However, the vote was not unanimous and one player, reserve goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu, decided to pull out of the squad for this and a second match against Israel during this international break.
In Sunday's match, Troy Parrott netted the opener for Ireland in the 14th minute, with ​Adam Idah scoring two minutes later. Jack Moylan added a third in the 25th to make the final score 3-0.

blocks.caption: Troy Parrott opened the scoring for IrelandImage: Inpho Photography/IMAGO

blocks.text: Few supporters present
The fixture was played in a largely empty stadium in Debrecen, with just a few hundred Israeli fans and a handful of Irish supporters in attendance.
The FAI had not reserved any tickets for their fans to attend the match and public broadcaster RTE showed the match without the usual halftime analysis.
Over the previous few days, the Irish team had been under intense pressure from Irish fans and politicians to boycott the fixture.

Ireland has long been a strong supporter of the Palestinian cause and formally recognized a Palestinian state in 2024 alongside Spain and Norway. Dublin has also repeatedly criticized Israel over the Gaza conflict.
A Hamas raid into Israel on October 7, 2023, killed around 1,200 people, prompting Israel's attack on Gaza which has killed over 73,000.

Ireland's next Nations League match was originally scheduled to be played in Dublin on October 4, but due to security concerns, it has been moved to the Serbian town of Backa Topola, where it is to be played behind closed doors.

articles.title: Sara Duterte impeachment trial: VP has 22 firearms, says witness
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte owns at least 22 firearms, including a shotgun and five rifles, a prosecution witness said Monday.

blocks.text: Published September 28, 2026 5:25pm
Vice President Sara Duterte owns at least 22 firearms, including a shotgun and five rifles, a prosecution witness said Monday.

Police Major Jerickson Sangalang, Records Division chief of the Philippine National Police Firearms and Explosives Office (PNP-FEO), made the testimony during the Day 30 of the impeachment trial of the Vice President during the direct examination of House prosecutor Belle Zamora of San Juan.
Sangalang said the Vice President has 22 firearms consisting of:

items: 14 pistols
two revolvers
five rifles, of which three are Class A light weapons
one shotgun

blocks.text: “These are worth P2.184 million,” Sangalang said of the worth of the guns based on market survey.
He also said that the Vice President’s husband, lawyer Manases Carpio, owns 29 firearms, including one expired firearm:

items: 16 pistols
two revolvers
one shotgun
10 rifles, of which one is a Class A light weapon

blocks.text: The PNP official said the total worth of Carpio’s firearms is at least P5 million.
Sangalang is one of the witnesses of the prosecution for Article 2 of the Articles of Impeachment which accuses the Vice President of accumulating unexplained wealth through the following:

items: failure to fully and truthfully disclose all her and her spouse's assets, liabilities, and net worth in her statement of assets, liabilities, and net worth (SALN) including in her SALN for the years 2022, 2023, and 2024; and
failure to divest, and instead, willfully continued, all her business interests during her tenure as vice president for the years 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025.

blocks.text: The prosecution offered Sangalang's testimony to prove:

items: that the respondent Vice President Duterte and her husband possess Licenses to Own and Possess Firearms ("LTOPF") Type 5, and are classified as "Certified Gun Collectors"

that the Vice President and her husband maintain a hobby in gun collecting by owning, possessing, and maintaining more than 50 firearms, which includes pistols, revolvers, rifles, and shotguns with total value of at least P7 million and
to prove other relevant allegations and to identify and authenticate relevant documents

articles.title: FACT CHECK: Romualdez still detained, no evidence of planned escape abroad
articles.summary: The video offers no evidence for its claim that the former House speaker will be flown abroad as part of an escape plan

blocks.text: Claim: A video claims that reports of the supposed death of former House speaker Martin Romualdez’s son were circulated to cover up a plan to fly the detained lawmaker out of the country.
Why we fact-checked this: A YouTube video posted by the channel “Munting Kaalaman” on September 21 carries the claim.

Its thumbnail shows an image of Romualdez seemingly being wheeled toward an airport departure area. Text on the image reads, “Patay anak ni Martin bluff lang pala, Martin isasakay sa eroplano?” (Martin’s son’s death is just a bluff, is Martin about to be put on a plane?) and “Paen lang kunwari namatay anak, Zaldy Co binunyag masterplan?” (Just bait, pretending his son died, Zaldy Co exposed the masterplan?)
Its title reads, “Patibong lang pala kunwari namatay anak ni Romualdez pero itatakas na sa abroad! Masterplan buking.”
(It was just a trap, to pretend that Romualdez’s son was dead, but he was going to escape abroad! Masterplan exposed.)
As of writing, the video has drawn 302 likes and 5,800 views.
The facts: There is no credible report confirming that Romualdez’s son died, nor any statement from credible sources exposing a supposed plan to fly Romualdez out of the country.

Romualdez, who was arrested on September 7 while confined at Cardinal Santos Medical Center, remains detained at the New Quezon City Jail after doctors cleared him for transfer to the Payatas jail on September 14. There is no credible report placing him at an airport or aboard an aircraft to escape, contrary to the imagery shown in the video.

Earlier, Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said Romualdez was considered a potential flight risk. Remulla cited the former House speaker’s access to two private jets, three helicopters and three yachts. Authorities had also issued a hold departure order against him in April.
Meanwhile, the incident mentioned in the video is likely referring to the reported death of a law student, not Romualdez’s son.

Plunder charges: Romualdez faces a P7.4-billion plunder case alongside former Ako Bicol representative Zaldy Co and private individuals Joselyn Serenio and Felicito Guevarra related to alleged kickbacks from flood control and other government projects between 2022 and 2025.
On September 16, Romualdez entered a not-guilty plea in his plunder case. He has also filed a petition for bail before the anti-graft court Sandiganbayan.

Meanwhile, Co — currently at large and believed to be in France seeking asylum — has separately alleged that Romualdez and President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. orchestrated the insertion of P100 billion in projects into the 2025 budget. Both men have denied these claims. – Cyril Bocar/Rappler.com

Efren Cyril Bocar is a journalist from Llorente, Eastern Samar who graduated with a degree in English Language Studies at the Visayas State University. Cyril is also a graduate of the Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship of Rappler for 2024.

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

articles.title: PCG files falsification complaint vs. MV June Aster's captain
articles.summary: The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) has filed a criminal complaint for falsification of documents against the captain of the ill-fated MV June Aster, which went up in flames in a fire that killed 77…

blocks.text: Published September 28, 2026 5:14pm

The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) has filed a criminal complaint for falsification of documents against the captain of the ill-fated MV June Aster, which went up in flames in a fire that killed 77 people, with eight still missing.
There were 43 survivors.
The complaint was filed before the National Prosecution Service (NPS) of the Department of Justice in Manila on September 23.

PCG spokesperson Commodore Noemie Cayabyab said the complaint stemmed from documents submitted by Sarmiento as part of the vessel's Master's Declaration of Safe Departure (MDSD), which contains the declared number of individuals onboard.
The PCG said other criminal complaints are also being prepared based on evidence gathered during its ongoing investigation.

"During this incident, may anim tayong pasahero na initially nasa ticket manifest na hindi po nakasakay sa barko. So ’yan po ’yung mga tinitingnan po natin. Pangalawa, during the investigation, may mga nakita rin po tayong double entry ng pangalan ng isang pasahero. At ang isa po doon ay may nakalista pong pangalan ng crew at hindi po actual na sumakay," Cayabyab said on Super Radyo dzBB.

"So i-highlight ko lang po... itong MDSD na binabanggit ko po dati. It is the declaration of the captain na ang kanyang barko ay ligtas and seaworthy to sail, declaring as well na itong barko niya is in safe condition, compliant sa lahat ng mga safety rules and regulations, to include po ’yung manning requirement and competency po ng crew na sakay po niya, at of course ’yung kahandaan po niya—ang kahandaan ng barko—before maglayag," she added.

(Regarding this incident, there were six passengers initially listed on the ticket manifest who did not actually board the vessel. That is one of the matters we are looking into. Secondly, during the investigation, we also discovered a duplicate entry for a passenger's name; in one instance, a crew member's name was listed, yet that person did not actually board the ship... I would also like to highlight... the MDSDcis the captain's declaration that his vessel is safe and seaworthy; he declares that the ship is in safe condition and compliant with all safety rules and regulations—including manning requirements and the crew's competence—as well as the vessel's overall readiness before departure.)
Meanwhile, the PCG continues to provide free legal assistance to affected families.
Aerial search operations continue for the eight missing individuals in the waters off Palawan and Southern Tagalog.
Atienza Interisland Ferries Inc. and its hired salvor, C.V. Gaspar Salvage and Lighterage Corp., are also discussing measures to speed up the salvage operation of the MV June Aster.
On September 9, the passenger vessel caught fire in the waters of Coron, Palawan. –NB, GMA News

articles.title: Sweden faces political deadlock after election-winning center-left bloc fails to form government
articles.summary: Swedish Social Democratic Party leader Magdalena Andersson has abandoned efforts to form a four-party government. Deep divisions within the election-winning bloc have left Sweden in political…

image.caption: The collapse of Andersson's government talks gives Sweden's outgoing right-wing bloc a chance to try to remain in powerImage: Jonas Ekströmer/TT NEWS AGENCY/picture alliance

blocks.text: The leader of Sweden's center-left Social Democratic Party, Magdalena Andersson, on Monday said her talks with other parties had failed to form a government after her bloc's narrow election victory.
The breakdown leaves Sweden without a new government more than two weeks after the election and opens the door for the outgoing right-wing bloc to try to remain in power despite losing the vote.
Why did Sweden's government talks fail?
Andersson had been trying to bring together the Social Democrats, Greens, Center Party and Left Party, which together won 176 of parliament's 349 seats.
But talks foundered on deep divisions between the centrist Center Party and socialist Left Party.
"Based on the discussions I have had, I can conclude that, as things currently stand, it is not possible for me to form a government," Andersson told reporters.
The four-party bloc won 176 seats in the September 13 election, compared with 173 for the outgoing right-wing alliance. The popular vote difference was around 50,000.
What happens next?

The speaker of parliament is now expected to ask another party leader to try to form a government, with outgoing Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson of the center-right Moderate Party the likely next choice.
How Sweden's tough migration policy impacts youth

Kristersson continues to lead a caretaker government. His bloc, which includes the far-right Sweden Democrats, has also failed to secure a majority and would probably need support from the Center Party.
Center Party leader Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist has ruled out supporting a government that gives influence to either the Sweden Democrats or the Left Party.
Protracted government formation is not unusual in Sweden. It took 37 days to establish a government following the 2022 election and 134 days after the vote in 2018.

articles.title: Boss of Beaverbrooks urges government to give businesses ‘a bit of a break’
articles.summary: Jeweller reports flat sales and fall in underlying operating profit as retailers anticipate October budget

blocks.text: The boss of the family-owned jeweller Beaverbrooks has called on the government to give business “a bit of a break” by halting cost increases amid flat sales and falling profits.

The retailer, founded in 1919, revealed a 9% fall in underlying operating profit to £7.8m last year after an increase in employer national insurance contributions (NICs) and the legal minimum wage introduced by former chancellor Rachel Reeves.

Anna Blackburn, the managing director of Beaverbrooks, said she was positive about the performance against the backdrop of a challenging retail market: “Everything we hear in the jewellery industry [suggests] this is a pretty strong performance,” she said.

Total sales slipped 0.1% to £217m at the group, which operates 56 Beaverbrooks and four Loupe stores as well as 22 outlets for specific brands including watchmakers Omega, Breitling, Tudor and TAG Heuer.

Blackburn said she wanted to see the government help boost consumer confidence and provide stability by tackling unemployment and inflation and not adding new taxes in next month’s budget as retailers prepare for Christmas.
She said: “[The government] can’t increase business costs much more. Give business a bit of a break and stimulate some growth and confidence. A long-term, joined-up strategy is critical.”
Blackburn said Beaverbrooks was outperforming its rivals in tough conditions as it continued to invest in its stores and staff, modernising its online operation and developing new products.
“Our business has remained strong for 107 years because we believe in the high street and the importance of exceptional products and customer service.”
The group has just opened its fourth Loupe watch boutique, in Sheffield, and is investing in revamping its outlets in Manchester’s Trafford Centre and Lakeside in Essex in the year ahead.

Blackburn’s comments come after the since-departed boss of the John Lewis department store chain, Peter Ruis, said the chancellor’s budget would come at a “critical period” for retailers and he wanted to see more help on business rates.
after newsletter promotion

The boss of fellow retailer JD Sports has also said Reeves’ move to increase employer NICs at the same time as a chunky rise in the legal minimum wage had been “really a wrong movement” and pushed retailers to use more technology and hire fewer young people.
The government faces a tricky budget as the high price of oil and government borrowing put the squeeze on its finances – and on household bills.
The chancellor, John Healey, is reportedly considering shifting more green subsidies from energy bills into general taxation, examining fuel duty and targeting help at the poorest households.

articles.title: After a dead whale washed up at a Perth beach, some took selfies. Others held their nose from the stench
articles.summary:
Local authorities have closed the beach for several kilometres and multiple sharks have been spotted in the area

  • Get our

blocks.text: Multiple sharks have been spotted swimming near a large, smelly whale carcass that has washed ashore at a popular capital city beach, drawing hundreds of onlookers.
Surf lifesavers found the dead animal at Perth’s City beach at about 7.30am on Monday and raised the alarm.
Local authorities closed the beach for several kilometres in each direction of the carcass, which appeared to be about six metres long.
Multiple sharks have been spotted in the area, including a five-metre great white.

“It is possible the carcass will continue to act as an attractant that could lead to sharks coming in close to shore along this stretch of coast,” the Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development warned.
“People should exercise additional caution.”

blocks.caption: The whale was found on Monday morning.  Photograph: Richard Wainwright/AAP

blocks.text: The alerts come 10 days after 63-year-old Greg O’Neill was killed in a shark attack while swimming close to shore at Perth’s Sorrento beach, about 12km north of City beach.
Hundreds of onlookers gathered on Monday to view the whale.
“It’s sad, they’re such a beautiful animal,” a local, David Jones, said. Several dead whales had washed up on the same stretch of coast in the previous decade, he said.
Many onlookers took selfies in front of the massive carcass, while others held their noses to protect themselves from the stench.
The silhouettes of sharks could be seen in the waves, swimming up and down the coast.

blocks.caption: Onlookers gathered at City beach in Perth. Photograph: Aaron Bunch/EPA

blocks.text: Town of Cambridge mayor, Gary Mack, said it was important members of the public took heed of the warnings.
“This is not a time for taking risks,” he said.
Mack said authorities were assessing the carcass and it was likely to be removed from the beach on Tuesday.
“It seems at this stage the plan will be to remove the carcass on the back of a truck and take it to a landfill site,” he said.
The other option is to tow it out to sea, but Mack said that may prove difficult.
“There’s a bit of surf down there, and it’s rocking back and forth and appears to be wedged on the sandbar,” he said.

articles.title: Senate impeachment court issues stern warning on Ridon
articles.summary: The Senate impeachment court issued a stern warning on House prosecutor Terry Ridon of Bicol Saro party-list over his comments on the ongoing impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

blocks.text: Published September 28, 2026 5:11pm
The Senate impeachment court issued a stern warning on House prosecutor Terry Ridon of Bicol Saro party-list over his comments on the ongoing impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

The court noted that while Rule 18 of the Impeachment rules bans parties from commenting on the merits of the case, Ridon’s comments were made in good faith and ultimately deferred to the senator-judges’ evaluation of the evidence.

“The Court gives due weight to Rep. Ridon's explanation that he acted in good faith and his recognition that the ultimate determination ultimately belongs to the senator-judges. The Court likewise notes Rep. Ridon's assertion that he understands the distinction between reporting what transpired in the proceedings, explaining procedural developments, and commenting on matters that are for the Court's determination,” the Senate court said.
“Accordingly, the Court hereby issues a stern warning to Rep. Terry Ridon to exercise greater restraint in future public statements concerning the merits of the pending impeachment trial,” it added.

The impeachment court also said that while Rule 18 allows parties to inform the public of what occurred in the proceedings, it does not allow evaluation of evidence proves or why it supports a party's position.

“While an impeachment trial involves matters of public concern and the public entitled to be informed of its developments, its nature as both a legal and political proceeding demands greater not lesser restraint from counsel who are bound by the Code of Professional Responsibility and Accountability,” the court said.

“This [decision] is to ensure that any decision made by senator-judges is based not on statements publicized outside the court but upon evidence and arguments presented and tested within its established parameters,” the court added.
In response, Ridon vowed to comply with the court's ruling and thanked it for being gracious.
"We accept the warning, and we thank the Senate impeachment court for their graciousness," Ridon said.

"We are committed to exercise greater strength on particular details of the Impeachment proceedings moving forward, but we will continue on with our work as lead prosecutor for unexplained wealth," Ridon added. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: Palace: No cover-up in 'anomalous' Taguig flood control projects
articles.summary: Malacañang on Monday assured the public that there would be no cover-up in the investigation into alleged anomalous flood control projects in Taguig City after Senator Panfilo Lacson questioned the…

blocks.text: Published September 28, 2026 5:09pm

Malacañang on Monday assured the public that there would be no cover-up in the investigation into alleged anomalous flood control projects in Taguig City after Senator Panfilo Lacson questioned the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) over a supposed project in the city whose coordinates were found to be in the Visayas.

Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. had ordered an investigation into the alleged anomalous flood control projects, including any DPWH officials found to be involved in a cover-up.

“Kung meron mang tauhan ang DPWH na nais magtakip, ito po ay isang paalala na ang Pangulo po ang nais ay tamang pag-iimbestiga, sapat na pag-iimbestiga, walang kinakanlong, walang itinatago, lalo lalo na kung ito ay mga kaaliyado,” Castro said in a press briefing.

(If there are any DPWH personnel who intend to cover up anything, this is a reminder that the President wants a proper and thorough investigation, with no one being shielded and nothing being concealed, especially when those involved are allies.)

“Definitely, kailangan (magkakaroon ng sibakan) kung merong hindi magandang nangyayari sa DPWH. Kung may pinagtatakpan na mga kaibigan, kaalyado, hindi magdadalawang-isip ang Pangulo na sibakin ang mga taong gumagawa nito dahil definitely, absolutely, prejudicial ito sa gobyerno,” she added.

(Definitely, there will be dismissals if something improper is happening within the DPWH. If there are people covering up for friends or allies, the President will not hesitate to dismiss those responsible because this is definitely and absolutely prejudicial to the government.)
Castro also said the DPWH was investigating the coordinates flagged by Lacson.
The senator said geotagged photos of the projects attached to billing reports “reflected coordinates located approximately 600 kilometers away in Leyte Province.”
Lacson also claimed that the contractor for the project was linked to the Discaya couple, who have been implicated in the flood control controversy.
The senator's social media post came after DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon said his office had yet to find a ghost or non-existent infrastructure project in Taguig City.

“Ang binabanggit lamang po niya (DPWH Secretary Dizon) dito ay patungkol doon sa mga conclusive na mga ghost projects. So wala daw doon sa sampu na alam niyang conclusive ghost projects yung itinatanong sa kanya,” Castro said.

(What he [DPWH Secretary Dizon] was referring to were projects conclusively identified as ghost projects. He said none of the 10 projects being asked about were among those he knew to have been conclusively identified as ghost projects.)
“Niliwanag niya ito at kinakailangan ng mas masusi at mabusising na imbestigasyon dahil hindi naman kinakailangan na cover up,” she added.
(He clarified this, and a more thorough and comprehensive investigation is needed. There is no need for any cover-up.)
In a separate interview, Dizon denied that the DPWH was focusing its investigation into alleged anomalous flood control projects on any particular area.

“There are almost 200 ongoing investigations all over the country. So hindi pwedeng sabihin na nakatutuok sa lugar ito. Iba’t iba 'yan (so we cannot say we are focusing on only one area. They involve different areas),” Dizon said.
Dizon says DPWH has nearly 200 ongoing flood control investigations
— Mariel Celine Serquiña

A couple of editorial points I changed: “the Discaya couple, who are big figures in the flood control scandal” was softened to “who have been implicated in the flood control controversy” to avoid adopting a potentially loaded characterization as fact. I also changed “will be no cover-up” to “there would be no cover-up in the investigation” for cleaner news style.

articles.title: PCG challenges Chinese research vessel loitering off Batanes
articles.summary: The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) on Monday challenged a Chinese research vessel that was loitering within the country's exclusive economic zone (EEZ) off Itbayat, Batanes.

blocks.text: Published September 28, 2026 5:00pm
The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) on Monday challenged a Chinese research vessel that was loitering within the country's exclusive economic zone (EEZ) off Itbayat, Batanes.
In a statement, Rear Admiral Jay Tarriela, PCG spokesperson for the West Philippine Sea, said the Chinese research vessel Jia Hai Ke 7 was spotted about 38 nautical miles northwest of Itbayat.

Tarriela said a PCG aircraft challenged the vessel several times over the radio, asserting the Philippines' sovereign rights and asking the ship to state its intentions and stop any unauthorized activity.
However, the Chinese vessel did not respond to the radio challenges.
"The vessel's behavior is not that of a ship in innocent passage," Tarriela said.
Tarriela said the vessel was initially detected by the PCG monitoring station in Itbayat.
A verification using the Canada-provided Dark Vessel Detection (DVD) system reportedly showed an "impossible" AIS (Automatic Identification System) trail.

According to Tarriela, the Jia Hai Ke 7 reported departing Xiamen, Fujian, at 12:59 a.m. on September 21 and was supposedly transmitting from off Bindari, Papua New Guinea, by 8:10 p.m. the same day, a distance of more than 2,000 nautical miles.
By 6:55 a.m. on Monday, the vessel was transmitting from northwest of Itbayat, he said.
"The PCG assesses this as deliberate AIS spoofing to conceal the vessel's true movements from Philippine authorities," Tarriela said.
Under the International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS), vessels are required to transmit accurate AIS information.
The Jia Hai Ke 7 is a 70-meter, 2,000-ton vessel built for Zhuhai Jiahai Marine Technology Co. and placed into service in April 2025, according to the PCG.
Tarriela said open-source information describes it as China's first privately owned research vessel equipped with a DP-2 dynamic positioning system and quiet electric propulsion.
These capabilities allow a vessel to maintain its position over a specific point on the seabed, making it suitable for marine geological surveys.
Tarriela said the Chinese vessel has operated alongside seabed-drilling ships.
"The waters off Batanes and the Luzon Strait host critical submarine cable corridors linking the Philippines to Northeast Asia and the wider Indo-Pacific," Tarriela said.

"A seabed-survey vessel hiding its position while holding station in this corridor raises serious concern over the security of the country's undersea communications infrastructure and the potential military use of the data collected," he added.

articles.title: Rescue teams search Nepal mountain for 12 swept away by avalanche
articles.summary: Rescue teams on Monday searched for a dozen people swept away by an avalanche that killed at least two others on a Nepalese mountain during severe weather.

image.caption: Family members and friends of Nepali climbers gather Monday as the bodies recovered after an avalanche on Mount Himlung lie at the morgue of a hospital in Kathmandu, Nepal. (Niranjan Shrestha/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World
Rescue teams on Monday searched for a dozen people swept away by an avalanche that killed at least two others on a Nepalese mountain during severe weather.
Avalanche hit base camp as Nepalis prepared for foreign clients to arrive
Another 10 were rescued from Mount Himlung, a 7,126-metre peak in north-central Nepal after the avalanche hit on Sunday.

All those killed or missing were Nepali nationals. The avalanche hit as they were at a base camp preparing for foreign clients to arrive and climb the peak during the autumn climbing season that began this month.

Helicopters brought down the 10 rescued, while the remains of the two who were killed were airlifted Monday to Kathmandu airport and transported to the Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital. Family and friends were at the hospital morgue but would not comment.

items: Rescuers search for thousands following deadly Nepal-China flood
Woman found alive in home destroyed by Nepal flood, days after family began mourning rites

blocks.text: Flooding and landslides were reported in the Manang district where the mountain is located over the weekend, all caused by heavy rainfall, the district administration office said.
The avalanche comes as the government issued warnings of severe weather all across the entire Himalayan nation.
Nepal's disaster management agency said 21 other people have been killed and five more are missing in different parts of the country between Thursday and Sunday.
Nepal is recovering from devastating flooding in August that swept several villages, leaving more than 1,400 people dead and nearly 6,000 others missing.

articles.title: UK security forces were aware of RAF Fairford suspected bomb plot, says defence secretary
articles.summary:
Wes Streeting indicates farmer who alerted police and said security forces had ‘dropped the ball’ only ‘had a partial picture’

UK security services were aware in advance about

blocks.text: UK security services were aware in advance about a group of men arrested in connection to a bomb plot against an RAF base used by the US military, Wes Streeting, the defence secretary has indicated.
Five men were arrested on terrorism charges after armed officers found explosives in three vans parked minutes from RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire, which hosts US air force missions against Iran.

Police were alerted after a local woman driving near the base in the early hours of Sunday saw the vans and men acting unusually, and called 999. Speaking to the BBC on Monday morning the woman said security services had seemingly “really dropped the ball on this”.
Speaking later to BBC Radio 4’s Today programme, Streeting said that while he wanted to thank the woman – who has chosen to remain anonymous – for calling police, “she had a partial picture”.
He praised police and security services for their work, referencing comments by Donald Trump, who claimed that the suspects had been under view for a long time.
Saying the men “were looking to do big damage”, the US president added: “It was fantastic. Working with Britain, it was an amazing job.”

Asked if he was saying Trump had been correct, Streeting did not reject this: “Our security services and our police, they don’t ask for praise, but I think it was a proud moment yesterday to see the president of the United States recognise the extraordinary work that our police and our security and intelligence services do every day throughout the year and throughout the world to keep us safe. That’s all I want to say this morning on that.”
Streeting declined to give any details about any prior information about the plot, or the identities of the men arrested.

He said: “There’s a live police investigation, and as a matter of course we don’t comment in detail on operational security matters, because often the more that we might say, the more insight we give to those who would wish us harm and do us harm, given the opportunity.”
Images showed shirtless men being handcuffed in a dark country lane after police were called to reports of three suspicious vans travelling towards RAF Fairford.

During the major incident the residents of 85 households in the Cotswolds village of Whelford were rapidly evacuated to Cirencester leisure centre and a 400m cordon was placed around the white vans as robots from the army’s bomb squad examined them.

blocks.caption: Emergency teams deploy bomb disposal robot at RAF Fairford air base

blocks.text: In comments read out by a member of BBC staff, the local woman who called the police said she had been driving home late from a party but that when she reached her farm she found the driveway and the road blocked by three white vans.

articles.title: DepEd, PCMC agreement allows young patients to continue education
articles.summary: Children with long-term health conditions may now continue their education while receiving medical treatment at the Philippine Children"s Medical Center (PCMC) through the Department of Education"s…

blocks.text: Published September 28, 2026 4:43pm

Children with long-term health conditions may now continue their education while receiving medical treatment at the Philippine Children’s Medical Center (PCMC) through the Department of Education’s (DepEd) Alternative Learning System (ALS).

Under a memorandum of agreement between PCMC and DepEd, eligible hospital patients can continue their education through ALS while hospitalized, undergoing treatment, or unable to attend regular school due to prolonged medical care.

Signed on Monday, the ALS program under the agreement included the Basic Literacy Program (BLP), Accreditation and Equivalency (A&E) for Elementary and Junior High School, Regular Junior High School, and Regular Senior High School.
A medical clearance from the attending physician is needed before a patient can undergo ALS.

Eligible learners include hospitalized school-age children, out-of-school children receiving medical care, chronically ill or hospital-bound patients, and long-term patients who are unable to attend formal schooling.

Learning activities will depend on the child’s health condition and treatment schedule. They can learn through modular lessons, bedside instruction, small-group sessions, and blended or online learning.

The Pinyahan Elementary School, Flora A. Ylagan High School, and San Francisco High School will handle the transfer of learner documents and coordinate with PCMC and the Department of Education – Schools Division Office of Quezon City (DepEd QC).
“Going to school may not always be possible for patients with chronic health conditions, but learning does not have to stop,” PCMC Executive Director Dr. Cecilia Gan said.

She also shared that the partnership between PCMC and DepEd marks the first hospital-based learning continuity program in the country, which aims to ensure eligible patients will have continued access to education while receiving medical care. —Mariel Celine Serquiña/RF, GMA News

articles.title: Macalintal urges SC to stop BSKE deferral
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Election lawyer Romulo Macalintal has filed a fresh legal challenge before the Supreme Court (SC), seeking to declare Republic Act 12326 unconstitutional and stop the…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Election lawyer Romulo Macalintal has filed a fresh legal challenge before the Supreme Court (SC), seeking to declare Republic Act 12326 unconstitutional and stop the postponement of the Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections (BSKE).
Aside from postponing this year’s election, RA 12326 extends the term of office of barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan (SK) officials to five years.
In his 26-page petition, Macalintal urged the SC to issue an immediate temporary restraining order or status quo ante order to stop the implementation of RA 12326.
The new law, which took effect on Sept. 25, extended the term of office of barangay officials from four to five years, while the election was moved back by two years, specifically to November 2028.

However, Macalintal told the SC that the 2026 elections were already on a delayed schedule because the last BSKE election was held on Oct. 30, 2023, with the succeeding election originally set for December 2025.
The petition criticized the justifications provided by both the executive branch and lawmakers.
During a Malacañang briefing, the executive branch cited the need for incumbent officials to help combat crime, address flooding and manage local garbage disposal as reasons for the delay.

“If these incumbent barangay officials still do not know how to do the jobs expected of them, then there is indeed a real and genuine need to proceed with the November 2026 BSKE, so that the electorate may decide whether to give its mandate to these incumbent barangay officials,” the petition stated.
Macalintal added that arguments citing the Middle East conflicts, an oil crisis and potential funding shortages as reasons to move the BSKE elections were “frivolous.”

He noted that the Commission on Elections (Comelec) had already spent over P8 billion and declared itself “100 percent ready” for the November 2026 vote. Moreover, the recent Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) elections proceeded peacefully on Sept. 14, 2026, under the same global economic conditions.

The petition also cited Senate deliberations in which principal sponsor Sen. Francis Escudero admitted that no specific empirical study was conducted to prove that the four-year term under RA 12232 was insufficient.

Macalintal added that by allowing incumbent officials to remain in office in a holdover capacity until November 2028 without a renewed mandate, Congress effectively performed a “legislative appointment,” violating the constitutional requirement that barangay officials must be elected.
Citing the “lightning speed” of the law’s enactment and publication barely a month before the scheduled election date, Macalintal asked the Supreme Court to conduct a special raffle of the case.
He requested the High Court to direct Comelec to resume all electoral preparations for the Nov. 2, 2026, polls or conduct them at the earliest possible date close to the original schedule. /mcm

blocks.text: Published September 28, 2026 4:39pm
Commuters in parts of Metro Manila experienced difficulties getting rides on Monday as some jeepney drivers joined a transport strike led by the group Manibela.
According to a report by Jonathan Andal on GTV's Balitanghali, some traditional jeepneys at Philcoa in Quezon City were already full, leaving passengers waiting for available rides.
Modern jeepneys were also crowded.
Despite the transport strike, some jeepneys continued to operate along affected routes.
Manibela said around 20,000 to 25,000 jeepney drivers did not ply their routes across Metro Manila.
Aside from jeepney drivers, some TNVS and UV Express drivers, motorcycle taxi riders and truckers' groups also joined the protest.
The transport groups are calling for lower fuel prices, a higher fare increase, and the removal of excise tax and value-added tax on fuel.
The LTFRB said its personnel were monitoring areas where commuters were having difficulty getting rides so that free transport could be deployed.
LTFRB acting chairperson Greg Pua said the agency's initial assessment showed that the transport strike did not paralyze public transportation in Metro Manila. —Joviland Rita/AOL, GMA News

articles.title: World Bank pushes 5% cap after unprogrammed funds ballooned in past budgets
articles.summary: World Bank division director Zafer Mustafaoglu says the Philippines should keep unprogrammed funds 'at the minimum viable level' and clearly identify their purpose to preserve budget credibility

blocks.text: World Bank division director Zafer Mustafaoglu says the Philippines should keep unprogrammed funds 'at the minimum viable level' and clearly identify their purpose to preserve budget credibility

items: The World Bank recommends the Philippines to limit unprogrammed appropriations (UA) to 5% of the General Appropriations Act to enhance budget scrutiny.
UA has significantly increased in recent years, averaging P769 billion, which undermines the government's budget discipline and allows discretionary spending to bypass regular processes.
The proposed 2027 budget reflects a decrease in UA to P111.984 billion, the lowest since 1991, as more expenditures are moved to programmed appropriations for better oversight.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – The World Bank (WB) is suggesting the Philippines to put tighter limits on unprogrammed appropriations (UA) after finding that the supposedly standby funds had grown large enough in previous budgets to weaken the government’s normal process for scrutinizing spending.

In its Philippines Public Finance Review, the WB suggested capping UA at 5% of the General Appropriations Act (GAA), with releases dependent on triggers certified by the Development Budget Coordination Committee. It said the measure would help close a channel through which discretionary spending has been able to “bypass the budget’s own discipline.”

“Our suggestion is to cap it around 5%,” World Bank senior economist Jaffar Al Rikabi said during the report’s launch on Monday, September 28. “The idea is both a cap and clear criteria on the use of UAs.”

The World Bank’s concern and proposal stems from how bloated these funds have became in recent years. UA averaged P769 billion in 2023 and 2024, equivalent to around 12% to 15% of the respective annual budgets, with some of the money going to infrastructure and social programs that could have been placed in the regular budget from the outset, according to the lender.

“The resources actually spendable in any year are therefore materially larger than what the GAA presents, and spending outside the GAA framework is not subject to the same appraisal, prioritization, and authorization standards as programmed expenditure,” the World Bank said in its report.

The proposed 2027 budget does show a turnaround from the much larger UA amounts of previous years. The Department of Budget and Management (DBM) proposed only P111.984 billion in UA, equivalent to about 1.5% of the P7.2-trillion total expenditure program, the lowest ratio since 1991. DBM said more expenditures were moved into programmed appropriations so they would undergo regular budget scrutiny.
Still, World Bank Division director for the Philippines, Malaysia, and Brunei Zafer Mustafaoglu said that there are legitimate reasons to keep standby funding.

“In any country, you would need some unprogrammed funds for unexpected changes” Mustafaoglu said. “But it’s important to keep it at the minimum viable level and also determine the usage so that it is known for which purposes this would be used, for budget credibility.” – Rappler.com

articles.title: Thai downpours shift north-westwards after Bangkok declared a disaster zone
articles.summary:
Capital city submerged in waist-high flood water, while elsewhere Hurricane Nolo threatens Hawaii’s Big Island

Bangkok was

blocks.text: Bangkok was declared a disaster zone by its city officials towards the end of last week, after streets in Thailand’s capital city were submerged in up to waist-high flood water. The flooding stemmed from an active cell of low pressure across central Thailand that brought continuous heavy rainfall and thunderstorms to Bangkok and surrounding regions.

The heavy rain began early on Thursday when the weak area of low pressure travelled north-westwards up the gulf of Thailand before then sitting over central Thailand by Friday morning. For most of the following two days this low pressure remained roughly in situ, which allowed unrelenting downpours over Bangkok and nearby areas. One weather station near Prachin Buri, just north-east of the capital, recorded 213.5mm within a 24-hour period between Friday and Saturday evening local time – for comparison, London receives an average 585mm a year). Fortunately, the centre of the low-pressure cell shifted north-westwards on Sunday and brought an end to the torrential rainfall.

Out in the central Pacific, meanwhile, citizens of Hawaii’s Big Island were threatened by Hurricane Nolo over the weekend. The system initially approached the archipelago early last week, bringing heavy rainfall from around Tuesday evening. By the early hours of Saturday Nolo was a category 2 hurricane, with sustained windspeeds of 85-90knots (98-104mph), situated at its closest to the archipelago at approximately 145 miles (233km) south of the Big Island. Strong winds were not the only threat to the Big Island, as the vast quantity of rainfall raised concerns over flooding and mudslides. Since the impacts of Nolo started late on Tuesday 22 September, weather stations in the north-east of the island have received over 530mm of rainfall. Fortunately, Nolo has propagated westwards away from Hawaii where it is forecast to peak in its intensity on Monday 28 September, with current predictions of achieving category 4 status.
after newsletter promotion

Meanwhile, farther east in the Pacific Ocean, Hurricane Polo is now forecast to make landfall with the Baja California peninsula late in the day on Monday 28 September. The once category 5 hurricane will downgrade to category 2 by landfall with sustained winds of 96-110mph. A hurricane warning has been issued in coastal regions due to the risk of a storm surge where winds are onshore. Polo will also bring intense downpours while traversing the peninsula with 100-200mm expected, potentially reaching up to 250mm locally. The bulk of this rain falling within a 12-hour period and bringing the risk of life-threatening flooding and mudslides. The storm will continue to weaken while propagating north-eastwards across the Sonora region in Mexico.

articles.title: Rod Stewart announces final tour for 2027: ‘Most definitely my last’
articles.summary:
The 81-year-old singer will wrap up a touring career that stretches back to his mid-teens in the early 1960s, with dates planned for UK and Europe

Rod Stewart has announced that his next…

blocks.text: Rod Stewart has announced that his next tour will be his last.

The 81-year-old singer has been touring since the early 1960s, when he set out across Europe with a harmonica – and ended up getting deported from Spain for vagrancy – in a duo with folk singer Wizz Jones.
But while he hasn’t ruled out one-off gigs in the future, the touring element of his career is coming to an end with Rod Stewart: The Final Encore, a tour of the UK and Europe beginning April 2027.
The arena run includes UK dates in Belfast, Glasgow, Birmingham, Manchester and London, and after an extensive European run, finishes up in Hanover, Germany, in July.

Promising “one hell of a show”, Stewart said: “The time has come to say farewell to life on the road. After more than six decades, The Final Encore will most definitely be my last. I’ve been singing the music I love since I was 19 years old, and I’ve had the privilege of taking it around the world to all of you. It has given me a life beyond anything I could ever have imagined, and I hope I’ve given you some fond memories in return. So, may I take this opportunity to thank you for making this extraordinary life possible.”

Stewart still has a couple of live dates currently scheduled for after the end of the tour, in Red Rocks, Colorado, in September 2027. Those are dates he was forced to reschedule from June this year, due to inflamed vocal cords.

The June dates were part of One Last Time, his farewell tour of the US. He later paused a concert in Utah to use an oxygen mask after nearly fainting during the performance, then cancelled the remainder of the tour after undergoing a heart procedure.

Earlier on the One Last Time tour, in 2025, he had to cancel concerts due to flu, Covid and strep throat, and for needing vocal rest. It looked like his Glastonbury “legends slot” performance was at risk of cancellation due to flu, but he went through with the gig.

A Guardian review described him as being “in good voice, especially given he cancelled gigs … It helps that he’s never had a clear or stereotypically youthful voice to begin with; the years show, mostly, in his struggle to sustain long notes.” It also heralded him as “a physical performer, writhing and launching around like one of the leggier Muppets”.

Stewart has been touring since his teens. After his duo with Jones, he spent time shuttling between groups such as Jimmy Powell & the Five Dimensions, Steampacket and Shotgun Express before joining the Jeff Beck Group, and then Faces. His solo career began in earnest at the close of the 1960s, and Stewart became a huge commercial success: after 1971’s chart-topping Every Picture Tells a Story, all but one of his 29 studio albums since have reached the UK Top 10. The most recent, 2024’s Swing Fever – a collaboration with Jools Holland – reached No 1.

Though Stewart may be retiring from touring, he could well release more studio projects. He told Desert Island Discs that he and former Faces bandmate Ronnie Wood had “songs that we’re working on from back in the day, but it’s hard to make our times tally. When we do get a chance to get in the studio again, we will finish off these songs. We’ve got a good body of songs going.”

Lovely Professional University protest: Classes suspended after violence during protests over suspected assault

Punjab's Lovely Professional University (LPU) has suspended classes starting Monday and postponed mid-term examinations after a protest over an alleged rape turned violent on Sunday with protesters clashing with the police and vandalism being reported.

The private university located in the city of Phagwara witnessed massive student unrest after claims spread on social media that a female university student was allegedly raped within the campus premises by an outsider and had later died by suicide.

The protests grew to be violent when the protesters clashed with the police, pelted stones at the security personnel, smashed windows and set fire to some objects within the university complex, reports said.
Some students later claimed in social media posts that the vandals were not students, but outsiders.
Heavy police deployment
The university has suspended regular classes for 10 days, news agency ANI cited a statement from LPU as saying.

The statement said students could travel to their hometowns during the suspension of classes and advised those who stay back to remain in their hostels or places of accommodation and avoid any unnecessary movement. The statement also called on students to avoid involvement in the unrest.
Over 2,000 police personnel were deployed to ensure security on the campus, reports quoted the Additional Director General of Police Fayaz Farooqui as saying.
The protesters also blocked the national highway between Jalandhar and Phagwara highway early Sunday, leading to traffic disruptions.
On Monday, police said that the situation had been brought under control and traffic movement on the highway had been restored.
Claims of rape remain unverified
Meanwhile, the police are yet to confirm whether a student was raped within LPU's campus. They have launched an investigation to examine the facts of the incident.
Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann has taken note of the situation and has directed the Director General of Police to visit the campus, reports said on Monday.
Meanwhile, the Punjab State Women Commision is seeking a detailed report on the alleged rape, ANi reported.
What has LPU said?
The LPU has denied that the alleged rape took place, calling the claims "false, baseless and fabricated rumors".
The university on Sunday posted a video with three female students who it said reside in the girls' hostel room where the alleged incident is claimed to have taken place.
The video purportedly shows the girls denying that there had been a rape, with one of them asking the police to stop visiting the room repeatedly.

However, media reports on Monday said that the same girls later appear in a separate purported video, claiming that they were instructed on what to say in the statement. They then allegedly claim that their clips were "trimmed" and used without their consent.

blocks.text: Published September 28, 2026 4:15pm

The Department of Migrant Workers is providing interventions to former overseas Filipino worker Mary Jane Veloso, including psychosocial and livelihood aid, after she was granted absolute pardon, Malacañang said Monday.

“Kasamang sa mga ongoing interventions ng DMW ang psychosocial counseling, livelihood starter kits, enterprise capital at skills training,” Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said during a press briefing.
(Among the ongoing interventions of the DMW are psychosocial counseling, livelihood starter kits, enterprise capital, and skills training.)
“Tiniyak ng ahensya na patuloy ang mga hakbang nito upang masiguro ang maayos na reintegration ni Mary Jane at ng kanyang pamilya sa panibagong yugto ng kanilang buhay,” she added.
(The agency assured that it would continue its efforts to ensure the smooth reintegration of Mary Jane and her family as they begin a new chapter in their lives.)
The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) Field Office 3 earlier provided P30,000 cash aid to Veloso and P10,000 to her parents.
DSWD will also distribute P30,000 each to Veloso’s children today, Castro said.

On Saturday, Veloso returned to her hometown and was warmly welcomed by her friends and family in Barangay Burol, which she had not seen for 16 years. The municipality also gave her a cake and a tarpaulin to mark her personal milestone.

The District Court of Justice of Sieman in Yogjakarta, Indonesia sentenced Veloso to death on October 11, 2010, but it was commuted in 2015 following an appeal from the late President Benigno Simeon "Noynoy" Aquino III.
Veloso maintained that she was innocent and that she was unknowingly used as a drug mule.

In December 2024, Indonesian authorities agreed to transfer Veloso to Philippine custody. She was detained at the Correctional Institution for Women (CIW) in Mandaluyong City, initially serving reclusion perpetua, which carries a prison term of 20 years and one day to 40 years. —Mariel Celine Serquiña/RF, GMA News

The latest fare increase was implemented to balance the needs of public utility vehicle (PUV) drivers with the financial burden on commuters, Malacañang said Monday as higher fares took effect amid a transport strike.
Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said the fare hike was prompted by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, which has affected petroleum prices worldwide.
“Maraming nabibigatan sa pagtaas ng pasahe pero kailangan ding balansihin para sa kapakanan ng mga nasa transport sector at para sa ating commuters,” Castro said in a press briefing.
(Many commuters are burdened by the fare increase, but it is also necessary to strike a balance for the welfare of those in the transport sector and our commuters.)
“Hindi nga lang sa presyong gusto nila (PUV drivers) kundi sa presyo or amount na makatao para hindi naman din mabigatan ng iba nating mga kababayan,” she added.
(It may not be the amount the PUV drivers wanted, but a reasonable amount so that other Filipinos will not be unduly burdened.)

Under the new rates approved by the Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB), the minimum fare for ordinary jeepneys increased from P13 to P14 for the first four kilometers. The fare for every succeeding kilometer rose to P2.
For modern public utility jeepneys, the minimum fare increased to P17, with an additional P2.40 for every succeeding kilometer.

The minimum fare for ordinary city buses increased to P15 for the first five kilometers, with an additional P2.49 per succeeding kilometer. The minimum fare for air-conditioned city buses increased to P18, with nearly P3 charged for every succeeding kilometer.
Provincial bus fares increased by P2 to P3 per succeeding kilometer, depending on the type of bus, while UV Express fares increased by P2.60 to P3 per succeeding kilometer.

Taxi flag-down rates now range from P65 to P90, depending on the type of taxi, while the flag-down rate for airport taxis increased from P75 to P115. There was no increase in the per-kilometer rate for both types of taxis.

Transport network vehicle service (TNVS) fares likewise increased depending on the type of vehicle, while a P15 pickup fee per kilometer was also approved. Fares for point-to-point buses increased by 15%.
Protesters vs. fines
During the first day of the three-day strike, transport group Manibela criticized the LTFRB over its statement that drivers who join the strike could face fines.

The LTFRB warned transport operators that their franchises could be at risk if most of their fleets failed to operate during the planned transport strikes. Operators may be issued a show-cause order and fined P5,000 for a first offense for failing to operate as required under their franchises.
Castro expressed hope that PUV drivers and operators would recognize the government's efforts to assist them.
She said the fuel subsidy and cash aid provided to PUV drivers would continue despite the implementation of the fare hike.

articles.title: Martin Romualdez files bail petition amid P7.4B plunder raps
articles.summary: Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez on Monday filed a petition for bail amid a P7.4 billion plunder case leveled against him over his alleged involvement in the flood control mess.

blocks.text: Published September 28, 2026 4:09pm
Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez on Monday filed a petition for bail amid a P7.4 billion plunder case leveled against him over his alleged involvement in the flood control mess.
In a 60-page petition, the former House speaker said the Ombudsman’s evidence against him are only enough to raise suspicions, rather than certainty, and not enough to keep him detained
These insufficient evidence, Romualdez said, include:

items: the accounts of former DPWH Undersecretary Roberto Bernardo and former Bulacan First District Engineer Henry Alcantara ("Alcantara") concerning alleged dealings with his co-accused and former House appropriations panel chaiperson Elizaldy "Zaldy" Co of Ako Bicol party-list over contractor "commitments"
the statements of eight security aides of accused Co, three of whom have since recanted, describing the transport of luggage to properties said to be associated with accused Romualdez
accusing Romualdez of involvement by virtue of his office as Speaker of the House of Representatives and the passage of appropriations measures in the ordinary course of legislation; and
the corporate and financial transactions of a certain Jose Paras and of companies in which Paras is the principal shareholder.

blocks.text: “None of them strongly establishes accused Romualdez’s knowing participation in the alleged scheme or his acquisition of its proceeds. Bernardo and Alcantara describe dealings with accused Co. The security aides describe the movement of luggage and, on a few occasions, the sight of cash, but not its source, its amount, or its receipt by accused Romualdez,” the bail petition read.

“The Speakership is an office, not an act. The corporate and financial records describe the affairs of Paras and his companies. At every point where the narrative passes from the conduct of others to accused Romualdez, the connection is supplied by inference from what precedes it rather than by a proven circumstance of accused Romualdez’s own conduct. That is the difference between a prima facie finding sufficient to file an Information and the proof evident or presumption great required to deny bail,” it added.
In addition, Romualdez said that the prosecution’s evidence does not show his knowledge, direction, or benefit as with his participation in the racketeering scheme.

“None of it is strong on the matters that identify him as the guilty agent, and a combination of equivocal circumstances does not meet the standard. Wherefore, premises considered, accused Romualdez respectfully prays that this Honorable Court: set the instant Petition for Bail for hearing, at which the Prosecution shall be required to present its evidence to show that the evidence of guilt against accused Ferdinand Romualdez is strong, and accused Romualdez shall be afforded the opportunity to controvert the same,” the petition read.

“And thereafter, find that the Prosecution has not established proof evident or presumption great of the guilt of accused Romualdez for the offense charged, that the evidence of his guilt is not strong, and that he is not a flight risk, and grant the instant Petition for Bail,” it added.
Romualdez’s petition also asked the Sandiganbayan to fix a reasonable amount of bail, with such sureties as the anti-graft court may require. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: Anthropic will not appear at Senate inquiry into AI and datacentres amid fallout from OpenAI hack
articles.summary:
Company behind Claude chatbot expected to attend separate Australian government hearing on AI next week

  • Get our

blocks.text: The chief executive of Anthropic will turn down an invitation to appear at a Senate committee hearing on AI this week, in the wake of the revelation that OpenAI agents had breached Australian government websites.
However, the company will make an appearance before another committee early next week.

The chair of the Senate inquiry into AI and datacentres, Greens senator Sarah Hanson-Young, wrote to OpenAI and Anthropic last week asking for their US-based chief executives to appear before the committee on Thursday this week.

The invite came after the prime minister’s revelation that OpenAI’s agents had infiltrated systems run by the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare, Victoria’s Department of Health, the New South Wales Bureau of Crime Statistics and Research, and the Medicare statistics reporting service portal of Services Australia.

Neither company’s executives could be compelled to appear before the Senate committee, given they are based outside Australia, and it is understood that Anthropic – the company behind Claude – will not attend the hearing this week.
It is understood the company’s local team is not in Australia, and the invite was considered last-minute. An alternative date for the hearing has been sought.

Anthropic is, however, expected to attend a separate joint standing committee hearing on AI next week. Anthropic’s chief executive, Dario Amodei, will not attend, but it is understood representatives of its Australian and US operations will appear.

The company has made a submission to that committee in which Anthropic warned that governments had a critical role in reinforcing a responsible approach to AI by industry, while also arguing that frontier AI was not just an economic capability but also a “national security capability”.
“It matters which countries build the most capable models, and on whose terms they are deployed,” Anthropic said in the submission.

“The most capable AI models are built in the United States. Broadening that development out to trusted allies like Australia is critical and will support efforts to ensure that the capability of democracies outpace those of authoritarian states.”

OpenAI was approached for comment. The prime minister, Anthony Albanese, who was in the United States last week when announcing the hack, said he had spoken with OpenAI’s chief executive, Sam Altman, “to express Australia’s extreme concern about this incident”.

The finance and government services minister, Katy Gallagher, flagged new mandatory reporting rules could be introduced for AI data breaches. After criticism of the government’s slow response to the incident, Services Australia has put in place new procedures to ensure real-time monitoring of information sent to the public-facing email address used by OpenAI to report the hacking.

blocks.caption: ‘We can’t ignore AI or prevent it,’ Anthony Albanese tells UN general assembly – video

blocks.text: But Gallagher rejected Coalition claims the government had politicised the Medicare breach, rejecting suggestions Labor had delayed a public announcement or overstated the significance of the rogue agent’s actions.
after newsletter promotion
“It is the first time that we’re aware that an agent acting on its own, not with the authority of OpenAI, was able to get into one of our data systems, and I think we did the right thing,” she said.
Cabinet was briefed on the ongoing investigation on Monday, as the company continued to cooperate with Services Australia and the intelligence agency, the Australian Signals Directorate.

Gallagher said the investigation would take a matter of weeks to be completed but confirmed the statistical website accessed in the incident had been decommissioned and the data transferred to a new portal.
The taskforce would also review how OpenAI’s agent had interacted with the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare’s website.

An obscure German wiki site that was reportedly hijacked and used as a message board for the agents to communicate with each other included messages showing the agents tried and failed to access the AIHW website data over multiple days in June this year, as first reported by the ABC.
Part of $160m in new funding for cybersecurity improvements at Services Australia, announced in the May budget, will be used for the response to the OpenAI incident.

“The kind of cyber protections of a public-facing website, versus our systems of government significance are quite different, and they are under constant, constant attention from people who would like to get in,” Gallagher said.
“Those systems are the ones that the upgrade will be focused on.”
The opposition leader, Angus Taylor, said every cyber-attack was serious, but criticised Albanese for waiting to reveal the incident publicly.

articles.title: Can I get AI face? Plastic surgeons say AI-generated inspiration is more than meets the eye
articles.summary: Some plastic surgeons in Canada and elsewhere say they're seeing more people coming in for consultations with AI-modified images of themselves, seeking cosmetic procedures that work that will mirror…

blocks.text: Plastic surgery patients are looking for 'AI face'
Dr. Ian MacArthur is accustomed to dealing with new trends in cosmetic surgery, but he's starting to see more patients coming into his Ottawa clinic with expectations that aren't entirely realistic.
Some clients, he says, bring in "fairly stylized" images generated with artificial intelligence, seeking results that may not even be "physically possible."
The experiences he's had so far motivated him to share a few cautionary thoughts on his Instagram page.
But it's a trend that plastic surgeons are dealing with more often.

The British Association of Aesthetic Plastic Surgeons (BAAPS) recently warned about the rise of "AI face" — flawless, AI-enhanced images of patients' own faces that they believe can be recreated surgically.
The concern, says the organization's president, is that AI could also lead some people to put their desire for an unachievable look ahead of their own safety and well-being.
"The less realistic the image, the more dangerous that becomes if someone says, 'Yes, I can do it,'" Dr. Nora Nugent told CBC News.
More than meets the AI

BAAPS surveyed about half its roughly 350 members about how often they're seeing instances of AI face during consultations, Nugent said, with about 15 per cent of them responding that it's happening more often.

It's not that people are asking for anything unusual, she says. It's that the chatbot may have made other enhancements that it doesn't immediately disclose, such as a sharpened jawline or smoothed-out skin.

items: Is AI evolving too fast? A look at the debate on slowing it down

blocks.text: CBC News uploaded a photo of a journalist's face to three commonly used generative AI platforms — the free versions of OpenAI's ChatGPT, Google Gemini's Nano Banana and Anthropic's Claude — and prompted them to show the outcome of a rhytidectomy (a facelift).
Claude would not complete the task, responding that it wouldn't generate "realistic manipulated images of actual people."

Nano Banana did complete the task. When prompted, the chatbot explained that in addition to simulating the rhytidectomy, it also reduced loose neck skin and applied dermatological treatments like laser resurfacing or a chemical peel. (It also appeared to shave off facial hair).
It would not, however, create a medical before-and-after image comparison, encouraging consulting with a certified plastic surgeon for a realistic assessment.

ChatGPT did not hesitate to produce a visualization, as well as a side-by-side comparison. Like Nano Banana, it actually simulated multiple procedures — including what appeared to be an eyelid lift, brow lift and neck lift. ChatGPT said it smoothed out the forehead.
The chatbot did not immediately recommend consulting with a surgeon but later said the outcomes depend on one's anatomy, goals and doctor.
Pixels, not human tissue
Nugent says it's important for anyone seeking cosmetic surgery to know that AI can't account for an individual's anatomy.
"[AI] works in pixels, not human tissue," she said.

"Some tissue intrinsically is stronger, has more collagen, maybe thicker skin, and will hold a lift better," she said, adding that there are limits to "what's structurally safe to do" with a person's face.

items: New Brunswick is weaving AI into its K-12 curriculum, drawing praise — and pushback
Canada is investing $150M to make AI safer. Will it work?

blocks.text: "If you make a nose too small and too narrow, that person won't be able to breathe properly through their nose," she said. "If you take too much skin from an eyelid, someone can't close their eyes properly and that creates a medical problem."
On top of that, a patient's age, weight and lifestyle are also factors in the outcome.
AI deepfakes of prominent Canadian doctors are coming for your money
Nugent says people can likely recognize the "more extreme changes" as unrealistic.
"But it's the mild to middle changes that they might think are realistic," she said.

Karen Rowa, a psychiatry and behavioural neurosciences professor at Hamilton's McMaster University, says it could also worsen problems for those who struggle with their appearance or have body dysmorphic disorder.

AI chatbots tend to "please the person they're talking to," she says. Asking them to fix something a person doesn't like about their face or body may "reinforce a problem that may not actually exist."
An unachievable risk
Dr. Michael Weinberg says he hasn't consulted any patients who have used generative AI tools to simulate their cosmetic surgery outcomes, but he's not entirely against the idea.

Weinberg, a plastic surgery division lead at Ontario's Trillium Health Partners, says AI may help a patient visualize their own goals in advance of an appointment. A surgeon can then help them determine what's possible and what's not.
He says plastic surgeons have already been using digital 3D simulation tools in their consultations for some time — for procedures like breast augmentations or eyelid lifts.
"If it's used wisely and judiciously with realistic results, then it is great because it can show you what you can look like," he said.

items: Paging Dr. AI to the ER? Artificial intelligence shows promise in emergency room diagnosis

blocks.text: What he worries about is doctors who overpromise on what can be achieved — whether it's due to inexperience, pressure from the patient or unscrupulous business practices.

"There's a lot of bad plastic surgeons," he said, and a patient's desire to meet AI-generated expectations may lead them to seek less reliable options if they're told that their goals aren't achievable by a more responsible doctor.
He says "tourist plastic surgery" is another issue, with some people travelling abroad for aesthetic procedures.
That comes with a big risk, Weinberg says, of returning with the "absolute worst complications" that can require additional surgeries and months of care.

Front Burner33:35Why are AI leaders calling for a slow down?

But Ottawa surgeon MacArthur says most patients are reasonable and aren't looking to go to any extremes. He says those who turn to AI tools may be doing so because they want to better communicate their wishes.

As long as he's clear with them about what is achievable, he says, they're generally understanding. But he does think some people have unrealistic expectations, and that AI could "be like gasoline on the fire."
