articles.title: 'Thrown under the bus': Former defence chief's memoir lays bare his battles with the Trudeau government
articles.summary: Former defence chief Wayne Eyre considered quitting "several times" as he battled the Trudeau government over military misconduct, defence spending and support for Ukraine. His candid memoir recounts…

image.caption: Prime Minister Justin Trudeau shakes hands with Gen. Wayne Eyre, outgoing Chief of the Defence Staff, after his remarks at a change of command ceremony in Ottawa on July 18, 2024. (Justin Tang/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Canada's former top military commander considered resigning "several times" during his tenure in battles with the former Trudeau government over the sexual misconduct scandal, and the lack of commitment towards defence spending.

Retired general Wayne Eyre's new memoir, Into the Breach: A Soldier's Journey, also peels back the curtain on the internal debate that took place over how to end the convoy occupation of downtown Ottawa in early 2022.
The prologue to the book, titled The Accidental CDS, is a tongue-in-cheek reference to his unusual, unexpected rise to the position of chief of the defence staff.

Eyre was promoted from being army commander to the top job after now-retired admiral Art MacDonald stepped aside in February 2021 because of allegations of inappropriate behaviour. Those allegations never resulted in charges and MacDonald didn't return to the defence chief's job.
Eyre was left to navigate the wider sexual misconduct scandal and a flurry of allegations which engulfed several high-ranking military leaders — an experience he described as "soul crushing."
He candidly writes about how, in the first few months, he often questioned whether he was up to the task.
Eyre's memoir recounts a highly charged incident in June 2021 where he said he felt thrown "under the bus" by former deputy prime minister Chrystia Freeland.

At the time, Prime Minister Justin Trudeau and Freeland both publicly questioned Eyre's decision to allow the now-former commander of the navy, Vice-Admiral Craig Baines, to remain in his post after he took part in a golf game with former chief of the defence staff Jonathan Vance, who had been under military police investigation following allegations of inappropriate behaviour.
In Eyre's view, Freeland's criticism amounted to forcing the prime minister to choose between his deputy and his senior military adviser.

"If there's no trust between the nation's senior military leader and the nation's senior elected leader, one of them has to go, and it's not going to be the elected leader," Eyre said in an interview with CBC News.
Support from Trudeau kept him from resigning

The incident culminated, Eyre said, when he was on the phone with the prime minister to discuss the decision to retain Baines. He was just about to resign when Trudeau stopped him by saying he still had confidence in him.

After his initial criticism, the prime minister made a further statement of support for his defence chief — remarks Eyre had not seen when the phone call was placed. The crisis was defused, but the tension remained.
Former military commander Eyre says he thought about resigning 'several times'
Eyre served another three years after the incident.
Resignation crossed his mind "several times" as internal battles unfolded over defence funding and the deteriorating state of readiness in the military.
Ultimately, he decided to stay because quitting would have precipitated a further crisis in an already wounded institution.
"You've got to be very careful as a military leader about resigning. You can fall on your sword, but generally it hurts and you can only do it once," he said.

"Resigning is an inherently political act, which could further fray political-military relations, [and] would cause a momentary blip in the media cycle. But at the same time, [it would] cause significant turmoil in the institution."

items: Gen. Wayne Eyre stepping down from position as Canada's top military commander

blocks.text: Throughout his tenure there was a series of rolling crises including the various waves of the COVID-19 pandemic and Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine on Feb. 11, 2022.
At the time, the Trudeau government faced public criticism about its reluctance to approve lethal aid for the embattled Eastern European country. It was a struggle, Eyre acknowledged.
"What we experienced at that time was a collision of ideology with reality," he told CBC.
"The ideology being, we are Canada, we don't supply weapons to a conflict zone. The reality was, OK, this is coming, Ukraine is a friend, this [is] one way we can help."
'Lethargy to approve a new defence policy'

Eyre's book is littered with further examples related to Canada's mission to train Ukraine troops and the transfer of M-777 artillery, underlining his frustration with the government's seeming "inability to make decisions at the speed of war."
He did note there were times when Canada later outstripped its allies in the swift delivery of war supplies and equipment, such as Leopard tanks.
The overall sense of frustration came into sharp focus during Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's September 2023 visit to Canada, which included a series of speeches in Toronto.

items: Zelenskyy's 1st visit to Canada since Russia's war 'emotional,' say some Ukrainians

blocks.text: "Both the PM and Deputy PM Freeland gave bellicose, impassioned speeches about being strong and supporting Ukraine," Eyre wrote, noting the contradiction between the political rhetoric and the fiscal reality that faced the Canadian military at the time.

"I, like the handful of CAF senior leaders present, had a hard time reconciling these otherwise great speeches with both the billion-dollar budget cut that they had just inflicted on us and their lethargy to approve a new defence policy."
The deeper the war in Ukraine became, the more concerned Eyre became about the state of Canada's readiness.
‘Urgency is required,’ says outgoing chief of defence staff Gen. Wayne Eyre on Russia-Ukraine war

He described how, in June 2022, during the run-up to the unveiling of Canada's new policy commitment to NORAD — the by national aerospace command — no one seemed to know where $38 billion in funding was going to come from, or where it would be allocated.

"Most galling was the 'smoke and mirrors' funding approach, with billions already allocated for other military equipment taken away and reallocated, with most investments only coming years into the future," Eyre wrote.
"With confusion persisting several days later, I drew some government ire when I frankly told a journalist that the source of funds 'wasn’t clear to me.'"

items: Top soldier says military looking for 'clarity' on Ottawa's budget plans

blocks.text: Military 'compartmentalized' Ottawa convoy involvement
The memoir also sheds light on a passing reference that appeared in the public hearings related to the invocation of the Emergencies Act to end the convoy protest.

Former deputy defence minister Bill Matthews testified that the military prepared operational plans as a precaution, but they were dismissed due to significant concerns that deploying troops would escalate tensions and mirror the 1990 Oka Crisis.

Throughout the convoy protest crisis, Eyre was firmly opposed to the notion that the military had any sort of role whatsoever. He attempted to correct the public perception by saying there's a difference between planning and scenario spinning.
"We looked at various scenarios, and it wasn't planning because a plan entails assigning troops to task and warning at all levels and the like," Eyre told CBC News.

"No, it was more thinking about various scenarios, and what questions would we have to ask, what measures would have to be taken. But given the sensitivity at the time, it was very compartmentalized."
Most of the discussion, he said, revolved around the use of military tow-trucks to remove protest vehicles.
In his memoir, Eyre wrote: "At the time one of my staff commented, 'If you accomplish nothing else as CDS, keeping the CAF out of this mess is a singular achievement.'"
Canada 'on the right path,' Eyre says
During his final months as defence chief and in his departure speech, Eyre warned about how dangerous the world had become and how Canada needed to prepare.

Prime Minister Mark Carney's government reversed many Trudeau-era policies and has begun substantially investing in defence — taking the country to the NATO standard of two per cent of the gross domestic product.

Several European political leaders, as well as security and intelligence agencies have warned that the West is likely to face a major conflict with Russia and possibly even China by the end of the decade.
Asked by CBC whether he thought the country was ready for what may be coming in the next few years, Eyre said no.
"But we're on the right path, and we are getting there."

blocks.text: Prosecution counsel Terry Ridon makes a manifestation during Day 27 of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on September 21, 2026.

items: The impeachment court warned public prosecutor Terry Ridon for potentially violating the sub judice rule through his media statements.
Ridon acknowledged the warning and committed to exercising greater restraint in discussing impeachment proceedings in the future.
The court emphasized the importance of distinguishing between informing the public and making statements that could influence the case's outcome.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – The impeachment court issued a stern warning to public prosecutor Terry Ridon over statements he made in media interviews that have been flagged.
The decision came more than a week after the court formally asked him and private prosecutor Jay Tolosa why they should not be sanctioned for potentially violating the court’s sub judice rule.

“The court gives due weight to Representative Ridon’s explanation that he acted in good faith and his recognition that the ultimate determination belongs to the senator-judges,” the ruling released Monday, September 28, reads.

“Ridon is cautioned to observe the distinction between merely informing the public of what occurred in the court proceedings and telling the public what the evidence proves or why it supports a party’s position,” it added.
The court said Ridon is “placed on notice,” and added that similar conduct in the future shall be met with a more severe penalty.

“We accept this warning, and we thank the Senate impeachment court for its graciousness,” Ridon said. “We are committed to exercise greater restraint on particular details of the impeachment proceedings moving forward but we will continue with our work.”
Ridon said the “stern warning” is not equivalent to a first offense.

Ridon’s statements that were flagged include a September 14 comment made during a press conference, in which he said: “Hindi nasabotahe si Cabotaje-Tang (Cabotaje-Tang was not sabotaged).” The statement meant to assert that the defense team was unable to damage the testimony offered by former Sandiganbayan presiding officer Amparo Cabotaje-Tang.

Another interview clip with the media made on September 15 showed Ridon saying “Pasok sa banga ang SALN (Statement of Assets Liabilities and Net worth) ng pangalawang pangulo (The Vice President’s SALN is right on target).”
Prosecutor Jay Tolosa has yet to disclose whether the court has ruled on the show-cause order separately issued to him. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse breathes new life into the series
articles.summary: TOKYO, Japan – It has been a long time since Castlevania received a brand-new game, but Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse feels surprisingly comfortable picking up the mantle. Playable at Tokyo Game Show…

blocks.text: TOKYO, Japan – It has been a long time since Castlevania received a brand-new game, but Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse feels surprisingly comfortable picking up the mantle.

blocks.caption: Image via KONAMI

blocks.text: Playable at Tokyo Game Show 2026, the upcoming title puts players in control of Rose Belmont as she battles through a monster-infested Paris alongside her father, Trevor Belmont.
Set in 1499, 23 years after Castlevania III: Dracula’s Curse, Belmont’s Curse follows Rose as she takes up the family trade while dealing with a mysterious curse slowly consuming her arm.

blocks.caption: Image via KONAMI

blocks.text: Developer Evil Empire previously worked on Dead Cells and its Return to Castlevania expansion, and that experience shows almost immediately in the demo.
RELATED STORY: The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past makes Letten worth the return
Gameplay

Rose is quick on her feet, able to slide past enemies, backdash from attacks and use her whip to swing across parts of the environment or quickly close the distance on enemies. Movement flows naturally into combat, making encounters feel fast without simply becoming a matter of button-mashing.

blocks.caption: Image via KONAMI

blocks.text: Different weapons also change how Rose approaches enemies. The Cestus, for example, trades the more familiar swordplay for punches and uppercuts, offering a noticeably different way to fight.

Bosses feed into the Arcana system. Defeating The Fallen allows Rose to absorb its essence and gain the Holy Cross as a magical attack, suggesting that taking down major enemies will gradually expand her arsenal.

The Fallen itself provides an early test of Rose’s mobility, leaping around the arena and attacking from different angles. Slides, backdashes and careful positioning become important, giving the combat a fast but deliberate rhythm.
Exploration remains equally important. The map features branching paths and areas that cannot immediately be reached, giving players reasons to return as Rose gains new abilities.

blocks.caption: Image via KONAMI

blocks.text: Visually, Belmont’s Curse mixes 3D characters with richly layered, hand-painted environments. It is more colorful than older Castlevania games, but the dark corridors, stained-glass windows and familiar monsters keep the series’ gothic identity intact.

The short TGS 2026 demo only scratches the surface, but Rose’s mobility, different weapons and Arcana system already give the familiar Castlevania formula some new tricks without straying too far from its roots.
Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse releases October 15, 2026, for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch and PC.

articles.title: Trump-Xi summit: What wasn't said might matter the most
articles.summary: The most revealing thing about the summit in Washington may be what the two leaders did not say - and what we still don't know.

blocks.text: Chinese state media confirmed for the first time on Monday that the trade truce has been extended until 10 January.
The short extension ensures both leaders will meet again at major international gatherings later this year.
Trump will attend the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen in November while Xi is due to travel to Miami for the G20 summit in December.
It is rare for the leaders of the world's two largest economies to meet so frequently.
But Beijing had hoped for a much longer extension to the truce, making the two month reprieve a modest gain rather than a major breakthrough.
China did secure lower tariffs on $30bn (£23bn) of goods entering the US with reciprocal reductions expected from Beijing.
Chinese products heading to American stores ranging from toys to small household appliances to Christmas decorations will benefit from the lower tariffs.
The Trump administration also said Beijing would buy at least 10 million metric tons of coal annually in 2027 and 2028.
What is striking is what was left out.
There was no mention of increasing exports of China's rare earth minerals to the US nor was there any indication that restrictions on advanced US semiconductors would be eased.
The White House factsheet made no mention of Taiwan, but the issue was clearly a priority for Xi Jinping.
According to Beijing's accounts of the talks, Xi urged Donald Trump to formally oppose Taiwan independence and handle the issue with caution.
After their previous meeting in May, Trump revealed that Xi directly asked him if the US would defend Taiwan in the event of a Chinese attack.
He told reporters, "There's only one person that knows that, and it is me," and he raised the question whether it made sense for US forces to "travel 9,500 miles to fight a war" over the issue.
This time, Trump disclosed far less.
"We didn't talk about it too much," he told reporters over the weekend.
"Right now, it's fine. It's just moving along," Trump said. "He understands very much how I feel."
That silence may be significant.
Trump has previously described a proposed $14bn US arms package for Taiwan as "a very good negotiating chip" in his dealings with Beijing. The arms package has been on hold for months.
Adding to the confusion, US Ambassador to China David Perdue told Fox News that Trump had offered to sell weapons to Xi during the summit.
The State Department later clarified that US law prohibits arms sales to China and there are no plans to do so.

Beijing sees the self-governing island as part of China. Most countries, including the United States, do not recognise Taiwan as an independent state, but Washington is opposed to any attempt to take the island by force and is committed to supplying it with weapons.

China says it will allow more foreign financial firms, including American-backed banks, investment companies and insurers, to apply to do business and open offices in China. But any approvals will still be subject to Chinese laws and regulations.
The last line is key. China is opening the door, but still controls who gets through it.

Foreign financial firms have long complained that regulatory barriers, licensing requirements and concerns over exit bans make it difficult to expand in China, even when market access is technically allowed.
Beijing also said it was discussing ways to increase the number of flights between both countries, but neither side has explained how this would happen.
And despite giving visa free entry to visitors from more than 75 countries across the world, China has not extended that offer to Americans.

Meanwhile the US State Department continues to classify travel to China as a Level 2 advisory urging travellers to "exercise increased caution" because of the risk of arbitrary law enforcement, exit bans and detention.
So even though both sides are talking about encouraging business and travel some of the biggest obstacles remain firmly in place.

blocks.text: Streeting thanks farmer who alerted police to suspicious activity but says she only has a 'partial picture'
The defence secretary, Wes Streeting, has spoken to the media from the Labour party conference this morning about the incident near RAF Fairford.
Streeting said he was grateful for the vigilance of the members of the public who are thought to have helped alert the emergency services to the suspected terror plot.
He renewed his thanks in particular to the local farmer who rang the police after she reportedly saw “a large group of hooded and masked men” near RAF Fairford early on Sunday morning.
Speaking to the BBC, the farmer said she thinks “someone dropped the ball” by allowing the suspects and their vehicles to get so close to people’s homes.
Streeting told Sky News:

double quotation markThank you to that member of the public. She has done exactly what we would hope that someone in that extraordinary situation would do. I’m really grateful to her – I think she acted, by her own admission, quickly and thoughtfully, and she did the right thing. With respect, though, she does only have a partial picture. And that’s as far as I wish to go this morning.

blocks.text: Police investigate possible Iran link to suspected bomb plot

Good morning and welcome to our coverage of events at RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire as counter-terrorism police investigate whether Iran is behind a suspected bomb plot at the base which is used by the US military to carry out missions in the Middle East.
Five men detained near the base early on Sunday were initially detained over explosives offences and then were further arrested later in the day on suspicion of the preparation of a terrorist act.

It came after armed officers found explosives on three vans parked minutes from the base. The suspected plot appears to have been foiled by chance when a local farmer spotted unusual behaviour late at night in the countryside from a group of men and called 999.
Dozens of households in the Cotswolds village of Whelford were subsequently evacuated during the operation and have still not returned to their home. Stay with us for further developments.

articles.title: Sara Duterte trial recap, Sept. 28: 51 firearms, GenCorp contracts
articles.summary: The unfurling of evidence in the trial of the vice president has appeared to slow down in the eyes of some senator-judges.

blocks.text: September 28, 2026 | 3:52pm

MANILA, Philippines — A police official testified Monday, September 28, that 51 firearms with a combined market value of more than P7.2 million are registered to Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband, lawyer Manases Carpio.
This was shared by prosecution witness Police Maj. Joericson Sanggalang, records chief of the Philippine National Police's firearms and explosives office, during the impeachment trial on Monday.

The unfurling of evidence in the trial of the vice president, however, has appeared to slow down in the eyes of some senator-judges. Sen. Migz Zubiri at one point likened the prosecution's recent presentation of evidence as a "big firework" fizzling out into a "kwitis (small rocket)."

Prior to the direct examination of Sanggalang, Zubiri and other senator-judges asked the prosecution why it deemed relevant to present a witness who will testify to Duterte's firearms, for Article II, which accuses her of possessing unexplained wealth.
Presiding Officer Sen. Chiz Escudero eventually allowed the prosecution to complete its presentation of the witness but asked it to shorten its line of questioning.
Here are the three highlights from today's proceedings.
1. Police official testifies on VP's firearms

At least 22 firearms are registered to Duterte and 29 to Carpio, Sanggalang said during the direct examination, led by House prosecutor Rep. Ysabel Zamora (San Juan). He put the market value of the vice president's firearms at P2,184,550.
Sanggalang said three of Duterte's rifles are Class A light weapons, which have fully automatic functions.

He said the firearms law allows law enforcement agencies such as the PNP and the Armed Forces of the Philippines to acquire such weapons. Individuals who owned them before the law took effect may keep them registered.

Sens. Zubiri, Erwin Tulfo, Tito Sotto, and Alan Cayetano questioned the relevance of the testimony. Zubiri and Sotto said officials commonly declare firearms as personal property in their statements of assets, liabilities, and net worth (SALN). "Many of us are firearms owners here, if not all members of the Senate," Zubiri said.
Sen. Raffy Tulfo later called the testimony "a waste of time."

Escudero, prior to making a ruling, said he himself was "headed towards excluding this witness." He noted that P7 million would be "well within the SALN [Duterte] submitted of P88 million as of the latest."
Zamora said however SALN guidelines require registered firearms to be declared individually. The defense said those guidelines apply only to SALNs filed from 2026.
Escudero decided to press on with Sanggalang's presentation but, like other senators, was candid in expressing his doubts on its relevance to the impeachment case.
"We find this witness not as convincing with respect to ill-gotten wealth as would be others," Escudero said.
Sanggalang confirmed that the values presented before the court were based on current market prices, not on the actual acquisition cost.
The defense did not cross-examine him.
2. PhilGEPS official: 11 of 15 Davao City contracts with GenCorp not publicly bid

During the first half of the proceedings today, Sopeña told Sen. Risa Hontiveros that 11 of the 15 Davao City contracts with GenCorp went through negotiated small value procurement. That method is used for low-value contracts and does not require public bidding.
He estimated the 11 contracts at P7 million to P8 million in total, out of about P34 million in Davao City contracts with the company.
Sopeña said none of the 11 exceeded P2 million. He said all carried the title "food and catering services" but were published and awarded on different dates.
Under cross-examination by defense counsel Roberto Batungbacal, Sopeña confirmed that 34 of GenCorp's 49 contracts were awarded by PhilHealth Region 11 and OWWA Region 11, not by Davao City.
Lead prosecutor Rep. Jinky Luistro argued that GenCorp's participation in the city's bidding was a conflict of interest under Article VII, Section 13 of the Constitution.

Escudero noted that Duterte's SALN declares her a GenCorp stockholder, while Securities and Exchange Commission Director Gerardo Del Rosario previously testified that the company's records do not list her.
"So that is one difference that still has to be reconciled at some point," Escudero said.
He said he expects both sides to address the discrepancy.
Sen. Ping Lacson meanwhile urged the defense to reconsider its approach of relying purely on technical questions, as these were not registering well with senator-judges.
The questions suggest the standard is proof beyond reasonable doubt, the level required in criminal cases, "which I believe is not the case in this impeachment trial," Lacson said.
3. Baste Duterte to testify Tuesday; rulings due
Escudero granted Davao Mayor Baste Duterte's request to testify on Tuesday and Wednesday instead of Monday.
In a letter, the mayor said he needed time to gather, organize, authenticate, and reproduce the documents covered by his subpoena, including contracts that Davao entered with GenCorp.
The prosecution also dropped PhilHealth witness Gary Samonte, a lawyer.

The court will rule Tuesday on the prosecution's request for admission on Duterte's bank records and other documents. A request for admission asks the other side to admit or deny matters so they need not be proven through witnesses.

Rep. Chel Diokno said the request would spare the court from hearing 20 more witnesses. However, lead defense counsel Sheila Sison argued that it runs against the constitutional right to remain silent.
The court will also rule on show cause orders issued last week to certain House prosecutors under the sub judice rule, which restricts public comment on pending cases.
After Baste Duterte, the prosecution will present two Davao City register of deeds officials and Atty. Ronnel Buenaventura, executive director of the Anti-Money Laundering Council Secretariat.
Whole-day trials begin October 1.

articles.title: Raffy Tulfo wants review of gun ownership law
articles.summary: Senator Raffy Tulfo on Monday called for a review of the country"s gun ownership laws after learning during the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte that an individual may own an…

blocks.text: SARA DUTERTE IMPEACHMENT TRIAL
Published September 28, 2026 3:45pm

Senator Raffy Tulfo on Monday called for a review of the country’s gun ownership laws after learning during the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte that an individual may own an "unlimited" number of firearms for as long as they meet certain conditions.

Tulfo raised the issue after prosecution witness Police Major Jerickson Sangalang, chief of the Records Division of the Philippine National Police Firearms and Explosives Office (PNP-FEO), testified that at least 22 firearms, including a shotgun and five rifles, are registered under the names of Duterte and her husband, lawyer Manases Carpio.
Sangalang gave the information during his testimony on the 30th day of the impeachment trial.

“Nagtataka lang ako. Hindi ko alam na puwede pala mag-own ng as many firearms as you can. Ang isang tao puwede na magtayo ng private army, puwede na magtayo ng isang army na lalabanan ang gobyerno,” Tulfo said.
(I was puzzled. I didn't know that such is allowed. One person can build a private army, even an army that could fight the government.)

“You can apparently own as many as one wants, up to 50, 60, 70, 100... Apparently, you’re allowed to do that. I didn’t know that. I thought there was a limit, certain limits [on guns] that you can own, especially high-powered firearms,” he added.
Tulfo said Congress should review the existing firearms laws to determine whether a limit should be imposed on the number of guns an individual may own.
“Whether you are a collector or not, there should be a certain number of guns that you are allowed to own,” Tulfo said.
Sangalang said there is no limit to the number of firearms a person may own as long as certain requirements are met.

“As long as they do not fall under Class A-type weapons, they may own them, provided they have an LTOPF Type 5 license. There is no limitation, as long as the firearms are properly registered,” Sangalang said, referring to the License to Own and Possess Firearms.

Under Republic Act No. 10591, or the Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act, Class A light weapons include self-loading pistols, rifles and carbines, submachine guns, assault rifles, and light machine guns that meet the law's specified characteristics.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Carlos Yulo and Chloe San Jose are engaged: ‘Blessed to love you’
articles.summary: Filipino gymnastics champion Carlos Yulo proposed to Chloe San Jose in December 2025, but the couple and their families kept their engagement private

blocks.text: SET TO WED. Filipino gymnastics star Carlos Yulo gives Chloe San Jose two engagement rings.
Chloe Anjeleigh San Jose Facebook page
Filipino gymnastics champion Carlos Yulo proposed to Chloe San Jose in December 2025, but the couple and their families kept their engagement private
MANILA, Philippines – The secret is out!

Carlos Yulo on Monday, September 28, revealed his engagement to longtime girlfriend Chloe San Jose just days after he won a pair of gold medals for the country in the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan.
Yulo popped the question on December 18, 2025, in Tagaytay, but the couple and their families kept their engagement private. The couple made it public nine months after.

“And all I can say and all I can feel, is that I am truly blessed. Blessed to love you. Blessed to be loved by you. Blessed to have you as my fiancé and, soon, as my forever,” Yulo wrote on his social media pages.
Yulo has credited San Jose for helping him become a more well-rounded person, saying that her presence and encouragement have enabled him to grow not only as a gymnast but also as an individual.
His growth culminated in a historic showing in the 2024 Paris Games, where he became the first Filipino to capture multiple Olympic gold medals with his triumphs in floor exercise and vault.
Symbolic of his two Olympic gold medals, Yulo proposed to San Jose with two engagement rings — one for each hand.
“Chloe really helped win the two gold medals in the Olympics. For me, she is the gold medal of my heart, so I gave her two engagement rings,” Yulo said in Filipino in their proposal video.

blocks.caption: Carlos Yulo and Chloe San Jose are engaged: ‘Blessed to love you’

blocks.text: The two began dating in 2020 after San Jose, a singer and content creator, reached out to Yulo to tell him she was a fan.
Yulo and San Jose remained together through a much-publicized rift with his parents, which intensified at the height of his Olympic triumphs.

“Neither of us could have known where that little message would take us. And from there, life became a collection of airports, competitions, hotel rooms, long training days, little adventures, big dreams, and countless moments in between,” San Jose wrote on her social media pages.

“I got to watch you chase your dreams and you let me be beside you through the biggest moments of your life. We grew up together. We learned together. We fought for each other, protected each other, supported each other, and built a life of our own.”
Yulo vowed to stand by San Jose for the rest of their lives.

“My love, I promise to always care for you, love you, and protect you. In good times and bad, in happiness and hardship, I will choose you every day. And, by the grace of God, I will be with you for all eternity,” Yulo said in Filipino.
Yulo returned home from Japan over the weekend after delivering the Philippines’ first two gold medals in the Asian Games.

He topped the floor exercise and vault as he finally completed his collection that includes gold medals from the Olympics, World Championships, Asian Championships, World Cup, and Southeast Asian Games. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Fact check: Graphic distorts Hontiveros, Diokno positions on school shooting
articles.summary: Gun access or online grooming? Both lawmakers have raised both sides of school violence.

blocks.text: September 28, 2026 | 3:42pm
Content warning: School shooting and violence
MANILA, Philippines — A social media graphic portraying Sen. Risa Hontiveros and Rep. Chel Diokno as taking opposing positions on school shootings is misleading.
In a September 23 post on X, a graphic compared the supposed stances of Hontiveros and Diokno, who are both affiliated with Akbayan, following a series of deadly school shootings in the country.
Diokno currently represents Akbayan in the House, while Hontiveros previously represented the party-list group and remains affiliated with the party.
A graphic shared on X portrays Sen. Risa Hontiveros and Rep. Chel Diokno as supposedly holding opposing positions on school shootings.
Screenshot taken Sept. 28, 2026, 12:35 p.m.
The image shared by X user @ALEXG00NCAYA0 shows Diokno alongside the statement, "It's the gun!" while Hontiveros' is accompanied by the text, "It's the phone!"
The graphic was shared with a caption favoring Diokno's supposed position over Hontiveros':

Chel Diokno > Risa Hontiveros for acknowledging the basic fact that the guns from shooters came from govt officials No guns, no shooting, no matter how much e-grooming you get. Social alienation will not be fixed through "child safety" laws, but through fostering community.
Rating: This is misleading.
Facts
The post presents a false either-or framing of the lawmakers' positions by presenting them as being on opposing sides of the issue following school shooting incidents in the country.

Hontiveros' position. Hontiveros called for tighter firearms regulation, saying the June 22 Tacloban school shooting may have been linked to online extremist group 764, which allegedly coerces children into violence and pornography.

In a July 1 hearing of the Senate committee on women, children, family relations and gender equality, Hontiveros said an alleged "adult groomer" may have recruited two minor suspects in the Tacloban shooting.
"Posibleng may mas malawak na network, at kailangang mahuli ito bago pa magkaroon ng susunod na mabibiktima," the senator said.
However, Hontiveros backed calls for stricter gun laws in an interview with ANC.
"I am also willing to bet na kung higpitan lang talaga 'yung pag-isyu at paglisensya ng firearms, mababawasan, baka makakalahati agad 'yung mga gun-related violence natin," she said on August 25.

Sen. Risa Hontiveros called for action addressing gun access, mental health, nihilistic violent extremism and the role of online platforms on Sept. 18, 2026 following a school shooting in South Cotabato.

In response to the South Cotabato school shooting on September 18, Hontiveros called to address different aspects that cause harm to the youth, which include gun access, alongside mental health, nihilistic violent extremism, and the role of online platforms.

"Panimulang hakbang na ang Sagip Bata Act na aming trinatrabaho sa Senado, na magpapalakas sa mga law enforcers sa pagsugpo sa NVE. But one measure will never be enough. Government needs to do a real accounting of how we are failing our children," she said in a statement on Facebook.

Diokno's position. Along with fellow Akbayan Party-list representatives Percival Cendaña and Dadah Ismula, and Dinagat Islands Rep. Kaka Bag-ao, Diokno filed a resolution at the House of Representatives to conduct a nationwide safety audit, inspection, and inventory of all firearms issued, owned, or possessed by government officials and employees.
Rep. Chel Diokno called for a nationwide safety audit and inventory of firearms issued, owned or possessed by government officials and employees on Sept. 24, 2026.

"Simple lang ang layunin nito: tiyakin na walang baril ang mapupunta sa maling kamay; panagutin ang mga nagpapabaya; at ayusin ang mga patakaran ng pamahalaan tungkol sa pagmamay-ari ng armas," Diokno said in a Facebook statement on September 24.

Are the two different? The positions of Hontiveros and Diokno therefore overlap on both gun access and the need to examine other factors behind school violence. The viral graphic strips away that broader context by presenting their views as mutually exclusive.
Why we fact-checked this
Three deadly school shootings have been reported in different parts of the Philippines since June.
On September 18, three students, including the shooter, died and six others were wounded in a shooting at Banga National High School in South Cotabato.

On August 18, two students, including the shooter, were killed in a shooting at Ateneo de Zamboanga University. Nine others were reported injured. Investigators said firearms linked to the shooter's father, a Bureau of Customs employee, were used in the attack.

On June 22, three students were killed in a shooting at San Jose National High School in Tacloban City. Later reporting placed the number of injured at 20. Investigators also examined how the minor suspects obtained their firearms and whether online networks influenced their actions.
As of September 28, the X post had garnered more than 300 reposts, 1,900 likes and 51,500 views.

articles.title: Sara Duterte’s gun ownership presented at impeachment court, but senators unimpressed
articles.summary: Sara Duterte and her husband Mans Carpio own more than 50 guns with a market value of over P7 million, the prosecution tells the impeachment court

blocks.text: VEEP. Vice President Sara Duterte addresses an event in Pagadian City, Zamboanga del Sur, in late May 2026.
Sara Duterte Facebook page
Sara Duterte and her husband Mans Carpio own more than 50 guns with a market value of over P7 million, the prosecution tells the impeachment court

items: The prosecution revealed that Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband own a total of 51 guns, valued at approximately P7 million, which were not declared in her Statements of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN).
The prosecution argued that the failure to declare firearms is significant in assessing unexplained wealth, emphasizing that public officials should fully disclose their assets, including firearms.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – The prosecution established before the impeachment court on Monday, September 28, that Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband, Mans Carpio, own a combined 51 guns, although it’s a fact that senators did not exactly appreciate.

The prosecution’s witness, Philippine National Police firearms office records chief Major Joericson Sangalang, confirmed that 22 guns are registered to the Vice President herself. Alongside her husband’s 29 guns, the firearms have an approximate market value of P7 million.
Rappler first reported about the Duterte family’s gun collection in March 2024.
The prosecution wanted to point out that Duterte did not declare her guns in her Statements of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN).
Senator-judges, however, tried early on to stop prosecutor Bel Zamora’s direct examination of the police official, questioning the testimony’s relevance.

“I have been reviewing my SALN also, and I do not see anything there that says guns,” Senate President Pro Tempore Tito Sotto said, saying he usually includes guns as part of the personal property section.

“Many of us are firearms owners here. We usually put it under personal properties. I don’t see there’s any violation that I feel would happen if they do that, if the Vice President had done that. I don’t think it has that much weight. We’re looking for the bigger evidence that they want to present, if any,” Senate Majority Leader Migz Zubiri added.

In defending the importance of the testimony, Zamora cited 2025 omnibus guidelines on SALN disclosure, which require individual declaration of firearms. Defense lawyer Carlo Narvasa, however, pointed out that the updated rules cannot be applied retroactively.
Post-trial, the prosecution justified its bid to present Duterte’s gun ownership before the court.

“Unexplained wealth is based principally on the SALN of the Vice President, and because she’s still married to Mans…. They should both declare whatever their personal properties are,” Kapunan said in a Rappler interview. “That includes firearms.”

“It does not matter the amount. Even when it is said it is only P7 million, when you submit your SALN, you are certifying under oath that’s all that you own,” Kapunan added. “This is where we attempt to show to the public and the impeachment court that there is a pattern from the Vice President of hiding her wealth.”

blocks.caption: Sara Duterte’s gun ownership presented at impeachment court, but senators unimpressed

blocks.text: Kapunan noted the hesitation of senators to discuss the matters because they are firearm owners themselves, but she believes the prosecution’s presentation shed light on the reality that a public official can have a private army.

“We can also segue into how relevant it is to grave threats (article). They do have a private army, and therefore it makes it more believable and more credible the article on grave threats,” she said. – Rappler.com

articles.summary: The Senate impeachment court has issued a subpoena to the head of the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) and two officials of the provincial government as discussions continue to revolve around…

blocks.text: Published September 28, 2026 3:27pm

The Senate impeachment court has issued a subpoena to the head of the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) and two officials of the provincial government as discussions continue to revolve around Vice President Sara Duterte's alleged unexplained wealth.

During the 30th day of the impeachment trial of Duterte, Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis "Chiz" Escudero said that AMLC executive director Ronel Buenaventura is expected to appear on October 1 to 2.
Further, subpoenas were also issued to two provincial officials to testify on the properties of Duterte's husband Manases Carpio.
Davao City Register of Deeds IV Kathy Florence Baldonado is expected to comment about Carpio's alleged property in Matina.
Likewise, City of Samal Deputy Register of Deeds III Marco Pineda is called to appear about a property in Island Garden City registered in the name of Carpio.
The subpoenas for Baldonado and Pineda cover September 30 to October 2.

The net worth of Duterte and her husband reached more than P98 million in 2025, an 11.46% increase from their 2024 net worth based on their joint Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN).
GMA News Research found that the Duterte-Carpio couple declared a net worth of P98,656,131.20 in 2025. The net worth they declared in the prior year was P88 million.
On the other hand, their declared total assets were P122,797,727.20, which is a 24.72% increase from the P98 million in 2024.
The Senate impeachment court is tackling Article 2 of the Articles of Impeachment, which specifically alleges that the Vice President accumulated unexplained wealth through the following:

items: failure to fully and truthfully disclose all her and her spouse's assets, liabilities, and net worth in her statement of assets, liabilities, and net worth (SALN), including in her SALN for the years 2022, 2023, and 2024; and
failure to divest and instead, willfully continued all her business interests during her tenure as vice president for the years 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025.

blocks.text: —AOL, GMA News

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has ordered the government to launch a nationwide communications program to help parents address online threats involving children, Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said Monday.

“May order rin si Presidente na nationwide may communications program kami para sa mga magulang para kausapin sila, para bigyan namin ng direksyon kung anong nangyayari. Everybody's at a loss na nangyayari dyan,” he said in an ambush interview.
(The President also ordered that we have a nationwide communications program for parents, to talk to them, to give them direction on what's going on. Everybody's at a loss on what's happening.)

“And the President has directed us to communicate of what needs to be done, kung paano dapat kausapin ‘yung mga bata, kung anong approach na dapat sa mga bata. And you'll get these materials very soon,” he added.
(And the President has directed us to communicate what needs to be done, how to talk to children, and what approach. And you'll get these materials very soon.)
Remulla said the program would provide parents with guidance on how to communicate with their children and respond to dangers they may encounter online.
He said Marcos’ directive came amid concerns over online grooming and other activities that could expose minors to harmful influences following a series of fatal shootings in schools.
The most recent incident was reported on September 18 in Banga, South Cotabato where at least three students were killed and eight others were wounded. —RF, GMA News

articles.title: Why Christian Esguerra was cast as Ferdinand E. Marcos in ‘Edjop’
articles.summary: 'Edjop: The Movie' director Katski Flores reveals why she took the risk in casting veteran journalist and content creator Christian Esguerra in her passion project

items: Veteran journalist Christian Esguerra was cast as Ferdinand E. Marcos in 'Edjop: The Movie' despite initially not wanting the role, believing it would have been better with a different actor.
Film director Katsi Flores insisted on casting Esguerra for his strong statement as an independent journalist, emphasizing the irony of his role as the dictator who suppressed media.
Esguerra's cameo included a significant line, and he underwent an acting crash course to prepare, but he expressed that he is unlikely to pursue further acting roles.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
He doesn’t look like the former dictator, doesn’t sound like him, and he’s not even an actor.
So, why was one of the country’s veteran journalists cast as President Ferdinand E. Marcos in Edjop: The Movie? (READ: [Rappler’s Best] The struggle against forgetting)

Esguerra himself didn’t want the part (he wanted a journalist’s role), and after watching the film last week, the former ABS-CBN correspondent and ABS-CBN News Channel (ANC) talk show host quipped the film would have been much better if another person was chosen as the dictator.
“I have to put this on the record, the film was almost perfect. Almost,” he said in a recent episode of his Facts First podcast with the film director, Katsi Flores.

“Ang minus dun, nagkamali kayo sa casting. Meron kayong kinuhang walang kwenta na hindi naman aktor. Pinaganap niyo bilang Ferdinand Marcos Sr. Yung lang ang pangit eh. Sabi ko, dito lang nasira yung pelikula. Okay na sana eh.”

(The film’s minus is, you made a mistake in casting. You chose someone who’s not good and is not an actor. You made him play Ferdinand Marcos Sr. That’s the only ugly part. I said, this is what destroyed the movie. It would have been okay otherwise.)
But Flores insisted she made the right choice.

“Let’s set the record straight. Pinilit ko po si Christian Esguerra. Sabi niya, ayaw niya, ayaw niya talagang gawin ‘tong role na ito, pero sabi ko sa kanya, kayo natin ‘yan. I just need like 20 seconds of screen time from you. I think it’s going to make a great statement,” she said.

(Let’s set the record straight. I forced Christian Esguerra. He said he didn’t want to do it, he really didn’t want to do the role, but I told him, we can do it. I just need like 20 seconds of screen time from you. I think it’s going to make a great statement.)

blocks.caption: CAMEO. Veteran journalist Christian Esguerra is Ferdinand E. Marcos in the film Edjop: The Movie, with (from left standing) Edgar Jopson’s daughter and film producer, Joyette Jopson; director Katski Flores, and film supporter, ex-congressman Lorenzo “Erin” Tañada III. Courtesy of Christian Esguer…

blocks.text: Esguerra, indeed, only has less than a minute of fame in the movie, but he delivered one of the most iconic lines in it when, after the young student leader Edgar Jopson, in a meeting in Malacañang in January 1970, urged him to to put on writing that he would not seek a third term, Marcos said: “Who are you to tell me what to do? You’re only a son of a grocer!” To which Edjop replied: “Honest grocer naman (An honest grocer, of course).”

blocks.caption: GROCER’S SON. The actual meeting between then-student leader Edgar Jopson with then-President Ferdinand E. Marcos in Malacañang in January 1970. Original image is from Edjop family archive; screenshot from Edjop: The Movie Facebook

blocks.text: For his cameo performance, Esguerra was made to undergo an hours-long, acting crash course with veteran theater actor, Ron Capinding. It helped that Capinding himself had played the role of Marcos Sr. in the 2023 play The Impossible Dream.
Had Esguerra flunked the test in the acting workshop, Flores said she would not have insisted on having him play the role of Marcos.

blocks.caption: ICONIC LINE. Christian Esguerra, as Ferdinand Marcos Sr., belittles Edgar Jopson, son of a Manila grocery owner, in the film Edjop: The Movie. Screenshot from Edjop

blocks.text: “Hindi ko naman icocompromise yung pelikula… Kung hindi ka naman nakapag deliver dun sa iyong instant audition, hindi naman kita ika-cast,” she said of her “passion” project that was five years in the making. “Paninindigan ko talaga yung desisyon i-cast ka,” she said in the podcast.
(I wouldn’t compromise the film. If you were not able to deliver in your instant audition, I would not have cast you. I stand by my decision to cast you.)
Elaborating on her decision, Flores said she chose Esguerra because she “wanted a strong statement, I wanted somebody who could provide an irony, be a talking point.”

That statement takes note of Esguerra’s record as an uncompromising journalist who is now one of the Philippines’ top independent content creators on politics with an influential following on social media.

After he was let go by ABS-CBN in 2020 as the network lobbied (but still failed) to get its broadcast franchise renewed, Esguerra quickly shifted to digital platforms and now has over 700,000 subscribers on YouTube and nearly 500,000 followers on Facebook. He hosts an almost daily Facts First show online.
Flores’ decision to use Esguerra as the dictator who shuttered independent media was also likely influenced by a changing media landscape here and abroad.

A global study, “Mapping News Creators and Influencers in Social and Video Networks” by the Reuters Institute and the University of Oxford says “news creators and influencers operating in social and video networks have become a significant source of news in recent years,” with Reuters Institute saying that “personalities and news creators often eclipse traditional news brands in terms of attention.”

The study’s Philippine case cites Esguerra as among the top 15 “most mentioned individuals for news on social and video networks by Philippines survey respondents,” a list that also includes Rappler CEO Maria Ressa.

“From the list above, only Christian Esguerra fits our definition of news creator in the political sphere. After a long career in mainstream media, he set up as an independent YouTuber and podcaster in 2022. His show, Facts First, aims to combat disinformation by providing facts and context on burning issues in Philippines politics,” the study says.

blocks.caption: Courtesy of Christian Esguerra Facebook

blocks.text: In Reuters Institute and University of Oxford’s 2026 Digital News Report, Yvonne Chua, an associate professor in journalism in UP Diliman, said that in the case of the Philippines, “About one-third of people (36%) report consuming content from creators or influencers mainly focused on the news. A larger proportion (46%) get some content from creators who mostly cover other topics but sometimes discuss current events.”
With actor now part of his resumé, will Esguerra be appearing in other films? Not likely, he said, but he joked that he hopes he’ll win an award for “Best Supporting Extra.”

As of Monday, September 28, Edjop: The Movie was still showing in four cinemas in Metro Manila: Gateway Cineplex in Quezon City, Robinsons Place Manila, Market! Market! in Taguig, and Ayala Malls Feliz in Pasig City.
The film will next be shown in select festivals in the United States and in Europe. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Children forced to give up school for work as fighting upends daily life in Yemen
articles.summary:
Renewed fighting between Iran-aligned Houthis and Saudi-backed Yemeni forces has shattered four years of relative calm

In the mornings, 13-year-old Muneer Farie went to school, and in the…
articles.byline: Nasser al-Sakkaf in Taiz and William Christou

blocks.text: In the mornings, 13-year-old Muneer Farie went to school, and in the afternoons he helped his father feed the livestock. He took his studies seriously, dreaming of becoming the first teacher in his family of farmers.

As fighting approached his village in al-Wazeyah district in Taiz, Yemen, two weeks ago, Muneer’s focus started to drift from his lessons. The classroom echoed with the distant sounds of explosions and gunfire. His home was suddenly on the frontline of renewed fighting between the Iran-aligned Houthis and the Saudi-backed Yemeni government.

“We heard there was fighting in surrounding areas but we didn’t expect it would reach our village that fast,” Muneer said. “As soon as the sounds of clashes approached our village, we took our livestock and important belongings and fled home early in the morning.”
He and his family fled south-west, moving to a camp set up for displaced people in al-Shimayateen, Taiz. They arrived penniless and lacking even the most basic supplies.

Muneer and his family are some of the more than 130,000 people displaced by recent fighting in Yemen, which started in September when the Houthis launched a renewed military campaign and rapidly moved south-west, seizing control of towns along the Red Sea coast.
The Houthis’ campaign interrupted years of relative calm that had prevailed over Yemen, with frontlines remaining broadly static since a UN-mediated ceasefire came into force in 2022.

The Houthis are now battling government forces and a Saudi air campaign to seize strategic highlands and supply lines on the outskirts of Taiz. Civilians have been driven out of their homes by the fighting, fleeing airstrikes and missiles.

Muneer and his brother, instead of studying, now sell socks and other cheap products in the markets outside his displacement camp. His classroom has been replaced by a small tent where he and his five siblings and parents crowd together in the humid night air.
He joins the more than 3.2 million children whose studies were interrupted by Yemen’s civil war prior to this month’s escalation.

blocks.caption: Displaced Yemenis carry water back to their makeshift camps. Photograph: Ebrahim Al-Suhaibi/Reuters

blocks.text: “Studying is important, but not in a situation like this where we are struggling to get enough food, water and other necessities,” he said. “For now, I will keep working until the war ends.”

His father, Ghaleb Farie, has been forced to ask his sons to work so that the family can scrape together enough to survive life in the displacement camp. Farie hopes the camp will be only a temporary home and that he can soon return to his village, but he is not optimistic as new displaced people arrive every day.
“What I was told by neighbours who have been displaced for longer is that the first few months are difficult and I will adapt,” Farie said.

Life has also grown harder for those who have remained in their homes. Abdulwasea Abdu, the principal of Musaab Ibn Umayr school in Taiz, tried to keep the doors of his school open for as long as possible to give children a sense of normality. But that normality was shattered two weeks ago when a missile fell nearby, exploding in sight of the students.

“On the day the missile struck, we witnessed severe panic among them, with crying and screaming due to the explosions. Some children showed psychological trauma as a result of the intensity of the blasts,” Abdu said.

The school was forced to close its doors, depriving the more than 600 pupils of their education. Abdu watches the battlefield developments closely, searching for a let-up that will let him resume classes, but so far the situation has been too chaotic.

“The area faces fighting from multiple fronts – south, west and north – which makes it difficult to take any steps toward resuming classes at the moment,” Abdu said. He fears that many of the children out of school and displaced will be forced into child labour.

blocks.caption: Children at al-Farsi camp for internally displaced people in southern Yemen. Photograph: Mohamad Hakim/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: The resumption of fighting has upended life for residents of south-west Yemen. Clashes severed the main road between the now Houthi-controlled port city of Mocha and government-controlled Taiz. The road is a vital artery for goods as it is one of the only in the area wide enough for large trucks and passenger buses.
Interrupted commerce has increased the price of basic goods, compounding the crisis, particularly for displaced people.

“It is civilians who bear the cost of military escalation, and it seems that we in Taiz are paying a particularly heavy price, as commodities no longer reach us easily,” said Essam Nabil, a 56-year-old carpenter in Taiz city. He added many people had begun giving up meat and resorting to cheaper foods.

The fighting has disrupted other, more mundane facets of daily life. Asaad, an expatriate who works in Saudi Arabia and asked to be identified only by his first name, can no longer take a direct trip back from Yemen.

“This reminds me of the early years of the war in Taiz, when the main roads were blocked and we had to travel through Aden before heading to Saudi Arabia,” Asaad said. “Now, we are repeating the same expensive and arduous journey.”

articles.title: Chancellor John Healey to promise ‘new age of industrialisation’ in speech to Labour conference – UK politics live
articles.summary:
Healey to announce new facilities to maintain nuclear submarines on the Clyde

Good morning. John Healey, the chancellor, is the main speaker at the Labour conference. He…

blocks.text: Good morning. John Healey, the chancellor, is the main speaker at the Labour conference. He was a surprise appointment to replace Rachel Reeves, he is unveiling his budget four weeks on Wednesday, and some of the pre-briefing suggests when the budget does come, it will be a relatively low-key affair, with a lot of decisions postponed until the spending review next year. And so we are definitely not expecting huge announcements at lunchtime today.
But there will be some striking language. Healey is going to promise a “new age of industrialisation”.
According to the overnight briefing from Labour, he will explain that in these terms.

double quotation markMy politics were shaped by the industrial heartlands of South Yorkshire. Today, on the site of the Orgreave pit, is Rotherham’s Advanced Manufacturing Park. Our coal mines are not coming back. But this is how Britain’s industrial past is being remade now for the modern world. This is the new age of industrialisation. A new confidence in Britain.
And he will also announce that the government is commissioning “three new floating docks for the Royal Navy’s submarine service at HM Naval Base Clyde” to provide maintenance for nuclear submarines.

Known as Programme Euston, plans for the new docks were first set out in 2023 and are expected to upgrade Faslane’s facilities for the next generation of British submarines, the Press Association reports. The Ministry of Defence has previously said they are expected to come into service in the early 2030s, and the docks form part of a wider £15bn upgrade programme for the Royal Navy’s shipyards.
Here is the agenda for the day.
10am: The Labour conference opens. The first main speaker is Wes Streeting, the defence secretary.
10.30am: Ed Miliband, the foreign secretary, addresses the conference.
11.10am: Jonathan Reynolds, the business secretary, speaks at the start of a debate on workers’ rights and reindustrialisation.
Noon: John Healey, the chancellor, gives his speech.
2pm: Heidi Alexander, the transport secretary, addresses the conference, in a debate covering transport and insourcing.

2.30pm: Yvette Cooper, the health secretary, speaks at an IPPR fringe event. Other cabinet ministers speaking at fringe events include Lisa Nandy, the culture secretary, at a Think Labour event; Pat McFadden, the work and pensions secretary, at an IPPR event; Streeting at a BAE event; and Ed Miliband, the foreign secretary, recording a What’s Left? podcast.
After 3.20pm: Alex Norris, the justice secretary, and Shabana Mahmood, the home secretary, speak at the conference in a debate covering crime.

articles.title: PNP witness: Sara Duterte has 3 firearms generally barred to civilians
articles.summary: Prosecutors allege the registered guns were not declared in Duterte's SALNs.

blocks.text: September 28, 2026 | 2:51pm

MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte has 22 firearms worth an estimated P2.18 million in market price, including three rifles classified by the Philippine National Police as Class-A light weapons, a PNP witness testified before the Senate impeachment court on Monday, September 28.

On the 30th day of Duterte's impeachment trial, Police Major Joericson Sangalang of the PNP Firearms and Explosives Office said records showed 14 pistols, two revolvers, five rifles and one shotgun registered to the Vice President.
Based on market surveys, Sangalang placed the combined value of Duterte's firearms at P2,184,550.
Three of her rifles were classified in the PNP certification as Class-A light weapons: a Bushmaster XM-15, an Heckler & Koch 416 and an Heckler & Koch G36.

Under Republic Act 10591, or the Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act, Class-A light weapons include rifles and other firearms not exceeding 7.62 mm that are capable of fully automatic fire.

The law generally reserves the acquisition and possession of Class-A light weapons for the Armed Forces of the Philippines, the PNP and other law enforcement agencies authorized by the president. It provides an exception for private individuals who already had licenses to possess Class-A light weapons when the law took effect, allowing them to retain and renew those licenses subject to other requirements.
Sangalang said the HK 416 is used by military units and estimated its market value at P900,000.
Carpio owns 29 firearms
Duterte's husband, Manases Carpio, meanwhile, has 29 firearms registered under his name, according to Sangalang.
These consist of 16 pistols, two revolvers, 10 rifles and one shotgun. One of the rifles was classified as a Class-A light weapon.
Sangalang estimated the total value of Carpio's firearms at P5,035,820.
Combined, the firearms registered to Duterte and Carpio were valued by the witness at about P7.22 million.
The prosecution raised the couple's firearms as part of Article II of the Articles of Impeachment, which covers allegations involving Duterte's alleged unexplained wealth.

House prosecutors have alleged that the firearms were not declared in Duterte's Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth and argue that their value should be considered in examining her declared assets.
The firearms issue was included in the prosecution's pre-trial brief. In June, prosecutors said they intended to summon PNP-FEO officials and establish the value of the firearms during the trial.

articles.title: Victoria police apologise over death of injured man taken to cells instead of hospital
articles.summary: Inquest into 2023 death shown footage of John Makai struggling to stand after suffering serious head injury from being punched in head by son

blocks.text: Victorian police have apologised to the family of a man who died after being held for five hours in a police cell without medical treatment for a significant head injury.
John Makai, a 58-year-old father of 10, died in 2023 from serious head trauma that went untreated despite him being unresponsive in a Broadmeadows cell, the Victorian coroner’s court heard on Monday.

On the first day of an inquest into his death, footage was shown in court of Makai being dragged from a divisional van into police cells, and repeatedly failing to respond when officers checked on him through the cell door.
The officers twice claimed that he had responded, despite the CCTV of the incident showing no such physical response, counsel assisting Rachel Ellyard told the court.
After the footage was shown, a lawyer for Victoria police’s chief commissioner, Mike Bush, said he apologised for the death.
Andrew Imrie, for Bush, said that Makai’s care “was not at the standard that … any member of the Victorian community is entitled to expect”.
He offered sincere condolences to Makai’s family and said it was “a situation Victoria police and all its employees work tirelessly to avoid”.

Imrie said there was a failure to complete a medical checklist when Makai arrived at the Broadmeadows station. He also said there were failures to notice his deteriorating condition, to complete a risk assessment, and to conduct adequate checks.
There had been disciplinary action taken against officers “where a basis was available”, he said.
“At this stage it is unclear whether these shortcomings would have made any difference to the tragic outcome in this case,” Imrie told the inquest.

The court heard that an ambulance was initially called – but was cancelled – after one of Makai’s sons punched him twice while the pair were drinking with another of his sons and a friend at a house in Sunbury.
Police attended the house and in footage shown to the court could be seen watching on as Makai struggled to stand and then collapsed into a bookcase while trying to sit down.
Police then had to support him to walk to the divisional van, and could be heard telling him to “get his legs up”.

When they arrived at the Broadmeadows police station about 20 minutes later, Makai could no longer stand, and had to be dragged out of the van by his legs, with his head seen striking the floor and walls of the van.
He was then placed seated on the ground, the footage showed.

Officers lifted him under the arms to drag him into a cell, where he was placed in what is known as a “coma position”, the inquest heard. He made no verbal response during this transfer, nor at any other time at the station, the court heard.

Police requested another ambulance at 1.25am, telling them that Makai had a minor facial injury and was in a very deep sleep because of his state of drunkenness, and they would like him to be checked by paramedics.
Ambulance Victoria told police they were struggling with workload but would dispatch paramedics when they were available.
“What was interpreted as deep sleep was in fact the increasing effects of traumatic brain injury and bleeding into the brain,” Ellyard said.

The court heard that because of an issue with Triple Zero Victoria, the job was not actually logged as outstanding. An ambulance was not dispatched until the same police officer again requested another five hours later.
The fresh call for an ambulance came after police entered Makai’s cell and could not get him to respond verbally.

“I’ve got a guy been in custody a number of hours, he’s breathing, trying sternum rubs, all sorts of … we can’t get any verbals out of him, we’d like an urgent check on his welfare,” the police officer said in a recording of the call.
“This request’s made since midnight, and for some reason it’s been cancelled at your end … I’m the custody sergeant, this guy’s breathing but we can’t raise any verbals from him.”
When asked about his breathing, the sergeant responds he had been snoring heavily but not responding “since he came in, since midnight”.
“Unconscious? And you haven’t had any response for six hours?” the Ambulance Victoria operator responds.
The sergeant then goes on to say his officers had been checking on him every 15 minutes, which Ellyard said was proven incorrect in a review of the footage.

When paramedics did respond, Makai was found to be showing signs of a brain injury, the court heard. He was transported via ambulance to hospital, where he was diagnosed with a non-survivable brain trauma.
He died in hospital two days later.
The first witness, Ryan Goon, the director of operations support for Triple Zero Victoria, said that the dispatcher wrongly cancelled the police request for an ambulance.
This was because of an issue with “multiple associated events”, as the first person to call for an ambulance at the Sunbury house had later cancelled the request.

Ellyard said the scope of the inquest – expected to run for two weeks – would consider the cause and the circumstances surrounding Makai’s death, including what treatment he could have received if he was taken to hospital rather than to a police station. It will also examine any changes to policies and reviews that had been completed after his death.
The inquest before coroner Paresa Spanos continues.

articles.title: Fuel prices finally roll back on September 29 after weeks of hikes
articles.summary: The price cuts are welcome news for motorists, alongside the renewed suspension of excise taxes on LPG and kerosene

blocks.text: A gas station in Manila adjusts fuel prices after another round of oil price increases, with partial adjustments already in effect, on March 17, 2026.
Rappler
The price cuts are welcome news for motorists, alongside the renewed suspension of excise taxes on LPG and kerosene

items: Starting September 29, fuel prices in the Philippines will decrease after three weeks of increases, with gasoline down by P0.24, diesel by P7.57, and kerosene by P5.85 per liter.
The rollback follows significant price hikes last week, driven by geopolitical tensions and disruptions in oil shipping routes, particularly in the Strait of Hormuz.
Additionally, the Philippine government has suspended excise taxes on liquefied petroleum gas and kerosene for up to three months to alleviate consumer costs.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – Fuel prices are going down starting Tuesday, September 29 after three consecutive weeks of steep pump price increases.
In a press conference on Monday, September 28, Energy Secretary Sharon Garin announced the following fuel price adjustments for the week of September 29 to October 5:

items: Gasoline – rollback of P0.24 per liter
Diesel – rollback of P7.57 per liter
Kerosene – rollback of P5.85 per liter

blocks.text: The rollback follows three straight weeks of increases. Last week alone, gasoline prices rose by P4.88 per liter, diesel by P8.82 per liter, and kerosene by P6.47 per liter.

Oil prices improved on renewed hopes for US-Iran diplomatic solutions amid the United Nations General Assembly meeting. Still, risks remain in the Middle East. Shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains lower than average, and attacks by Yemen’s Houthis threaten to further wreck Saudi energy infrastructure and Red Sea shipping.

The Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway between Iran and Oman, is one of the world’s most important oil shipping routes. Any disruption to tanker traffic can quickly affect global crude and refined product prices.
The rollback comes alongside another government measure intended to cushion consumers from high energy costs.
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Friday, September 25, ordered the full suspension of excise taxes on liquefied petroleum gas and kerosene. It does not cover gasoline or diesel.
The suspension may last for up to three months but will be reviewed regularly by the Development Budget Coordination Committee and the DOE.
The government previously suspended excise taxes on LPG and kerosene earlier this year before restoring them in July after the one-month average Dubai crude price fell below $80 per barrel.

Despite the latest rollback, local pump prices remain well above levels seen before fighting involving Iran and US-Israeli forces broke out on February 28. In the last full week before the conflict, DOE data showed common retail prices in Metro Manila at P56 per liter for gasoline RON95, P54.70 per liter for gasoline RON91, P55 per liter for diesel, and P83.47 per liter for kerosene.

The Philippines imports much of its fuel as finished petroleum products, making domestic pump prices vulnerable to movements in regional refined fuel prices, foreign exchange rates, and disruptions in international supply routes. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Venezuelans demand opposition leader Machado's return
articles.summary: Hundreds of people held rallies in Venezuela demanding the safe return of Maria Corina Machado, and fair elections.

image.caption: Supporters of opposition leader Maria Corina Machado demanded her safe return to VenezuelaImage: Pedro Mattey/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Supporters of Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado held a rally on Sunday demanding her safe return and for fair presidential elections in Venezuela.
Her supporters joined the rally wearing sky-blue shirts which is the color of Machado's Vente Venezuela party and rode motorcycles through the streets in Caracas.
Similar rallies were held in several state capitals including Valencia, Maracaibo and Merida.
"This is not a matter of parties or politics," said Flavio Valentini, a Vente Venezuela activist in Caracas who grabbed a megaphone and addressed the crowd.

blocks.caption: Machado's supporters rode motocycles through streets as they demanded a free and fair election in VenezuelaImage: Juan Carlos Hernandez/REUTERS

blocks.text: "This is a movement for the people and by the people."
The demonstrators demanded a clear timeline for presidential elections in 2027 and chanted slogans including "Freedom, freedom!"
Machado's return from exile

For the past nine months, Machado has been living in exile. Last year in December, Machado left for Oslo to receive the Nobel Peace Prize. Since then she has tried returning to Venezuela multiple times.
Machado, who is currently in Panama, has so far made seven unsuccessful attempts to return, according to media reports.
Activists allege the Venezuelan government keeps blocking her return, however, Venezuelan authorities deny the claim.
Venezuelans want elections — but when will they get them?
Courts had barred Machado from running in elections under the government of President Nicolás Maduro. But her stand-in candidate is widely believed to have won the election.

Maduro refuted the election results. After his disputed victory, his government led a crackdown against dissidents who protested the official results, forcing Machado and dozens of opposition leaders to flee.
The US captured Maduro in January. But Machado has been unable to return to Venezuela since then.
Currently, the country is being led by acting President Delcy Rodríguez, who has worked closely with Washington.

"We hope this transition process leads us to presidential elections and consolidates a free, democratic country that will be the main ally of the United States," said Anthony Romero, a leader for Vente Venezuela in the nation's capital.

blocks.text: Left Party politician Elif Eralp, who could become Berlin's next mayor after an election win last week, has filed a criminal complaint against conservative Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt over a remark referring to her as an "antisemite."

Lawyer Jasper Prigge told the DPA news agency the complaint by Eralp and the Berlin branch of the Left Party argues that Dobrindt endorsed a statement describing Eralp as an "antisemite" in what amounted to a criminal act of defamation and insult.
The incident occurred in a talkshow on German television on Thursday.
The moderator of the show, Maybrit Illner, said, "Elif Eralp says she is an antisemite," quickly correcting her slip-up to "... [that] she is not an antisemite."
Dobrindt then said: "Oh, yes, she is."
Dobrindt had said on an earlier occasion that the Berlin branch of the Left Party was "quite obviously tolerating antisemites and extremists in its orbit."
Eralp herself has repeatedly condemned all forms of antisemitism and reaffirmed Israel's right to exist.
The legal action comes as many conservative politicians have reacted with outrage to the victory of the socialist party in the elections on September 20.
Some observers, however, see the accusations of antisemitism levelled at the party as overblown and politically motivated.
