articles.title: What would Francis of Assisi make of his fame today?
articles.summary: The Catholic saint renounced wealth and fame to become a mendicant friar. Yet over history, his teachings and life have inspired popes, Dante, and even Mussolini.

image.caption: Francis of Assisi is best known for his teachings about humankind's deep kinship with the natural world and non-human creaturesImage: picture alliance / Heritage Images

blocks.text: One could safely say that Francis of Assisi's life — and afterlife — is defined by paradox.
He embraced poverty, yet lies entombed today in a grand basilica with frescoes by renowned medieval artists in his native Assisi in central Italy.
He advocated meekness, yet hundreds of thousands venerated his remains when they went on public display earlier this year to commemorate 800 years since his death on October 3, 1226.

blocks.caption: Thousands came to venerate the saint's remains earlier this year, amid wide media coverage Image: Emanuela Bianconi/IPA/ZUMA/picture alliance

blocks.text: So, why has this Catholic saint inspired papal encyclicals, ecological activism, global pet‑blessing rituals — and even the propaganda of former Italian fascist leader Benito Mussolini?
And what might Francis make of this fame that he'd shunned while alive?
From riches to rags

Born in Assisi — a hill town in central Italy — in 1181 or 1182, he was first named Giovanni di Pietro di Bernardone. But his father, a cloth merchant with trade links to France, renamed him Francesco.

Early Franciscan hagiographers — medieval writers who recorded his life and shaped how later generations understood him — describe him as a lively, sociable young man who enjoyed singing, parties and the privileges of wealth.

blocks.caption: The magnificent interior of the Basilica of St Francis of AssisiImage: Sepp Spiegl/IMAGO

blocks.text: However, he didn't want to join his father's trade; he dreamed of becoming a knight.

In 1202, Francis joined Assisi's forces in a battle against neighboring Perugia. He was captured, spent a year in prison, and returned home shaken and ill. This, and a series of subsequent events, precipitated a slow shift in his outlook.

One took place at the small, ruined Church of San Damiano outside Assisi, where Francis believed he heard Jesus Christ calling on him to "rebuild my church." Taking it literally, he began repairing local chapels. And when he ran out of money, he sold cloth from his father's shop, which enraged the latter and led to a dramatic episode in Assisi's town square.

blocks.caption: Norberto Proietti's 'The Return of St Francis' captures the saint returning as a dejected knight after his imprisonment in PerugiaImage: Gabriele Thielmann/imageBROKER/IMAGO

blocks.text: Before the bishop and gathered townspeople, Francis stripped off his fine clothes, renouncing his father, his inheritance and all material comforts. He committed himself to a life of poverty, humility, care for the poor and sick, and a deep kinship with nature.
A relatable saint
As a wandering preacher, he drew followers and eventually founded the Order of Friars Minor, known today as the Franciscans.

Widely considered the first saint to have miraculously received the stigmata — physical wounds resembling those on the crucified body of Jesus Christ — Francis was canonized by Pope Gregory IX on July 16, 1228. This unusually swift recognition amplified his fame beyond Assisi.

In the following centuries, Francis became one of the most frequently depicted saints in Western art, inspiring works from Dante's "Divine Comedy" to films, children's books, and even a 1980 Marvel comic.

blocks.caption: Cover of the 1980 Marvel comic on Francis' lifeImage: Marvel Comics Group

blocks.text: "Most saints are seen as unapproachable or unrelatable, but Francis' story of lifelong conversion and the desire to be in a positive relationship with others, God and the rest of creation speaks to people across time and cultures," theologian and former Franciscan friar Daniel P. Horan tells DW.

According to cultural historian Amanda Minervini, this broad appeal is also what made Francis so adaptable across eras: "In Francis, there seems to be something for everyone: the pacifist, the ascetic, the mason, the environmentalist, the minimalist, the lover of animals also loved by animals, the diplomat, the mystic, the radical, the performer, and even the model of a different kind of masculinity," they tell DW.

blocks.caption: Painting depicting Francis receiving the stigmata — the wounds of the crucified Jesus ChristImage: Heritage Images/IMAGO

blocks.text: Pacifist mascot of a fascist regime

His image has been reconstructed throughout history, points out Minervini, who has explored in their research one particularly jarring example: Francis' political appropriation by Benito Mussolini's fascist regime.

In their recent book, "St. Francis and Mussolini: Fascist Appropriations of a Beloved Italian Saint" (2026), they explain how fascist rhetoric manipulated Francis' stigmata, reframing them as symbols of heroic suffering and sacrifice. "The wounds of the saint were thus invoked to glorify sacrifice and inspire Italian youth to go to war."

Noting how Mussolini chose to be rebaptized in 1927 to strengthen his alliance with the Vatican, they add, "St. Francis offered a particularly useful means of conferring religious legitimacy upon political power."

blocks.caption: Italian leader Benito Mussolini (left), who in fact inspired Germany's Adolf Hitler, appropriated Francis' teachings to legitimize fascist idealsImage: United Archives International/IMAGO

blocks.text: Minervini's research shows that Francis' pacifism — "likely because he had known what war meant" — was deliberately played down. Their book reproduces a confidential note addressed to military chaplains in 1929, which expressed concern that they might preach ideals of peace to the troops.
"This document provides clear evidence that peace was an aspect of Francesco's legacy that fascist groups sought to suppress rather than promote."

Furthermore, after Italy — a former Axis power along with Nazi Germany — switched sides and joined the Allies during World War II, the latter were often willing to condone or overlook Italy's crimes rather than investigate its fascist past.
"In this climate, many fascists remained in place, and the politically compromised image of Francis was quietly set aside," explains Minervini.

blocks.caption: Painting depicting St Francis having an audience with Sultan Malik al-KamilImage: IMAGO/Heritage Images

blocks.text: Medieval peace envoy
Francis has however remained associated with peace-making.

In 1219, during the Fifth Crusade, he traveled with the crusading army to Damietta, a port city in northern Egypt, and obtained permission to cross into the Muslim camp and meet personally with the sultan, Malik al-Kamil. His aim was to convert the sultan and bring an end to the bloody conflict.

Describing his action as "an extraordinarily audacious thing to do," Minervini says the encounter did not produce the conversion or political breakthrough Francis may have hoped for, but his return unscathed ensured that early sources took notice of him.

Daniel Horan adds that despite Christians viewing Muslims as the enemy back then, St Francis "would not go along with that dehumanizing perspective" and instead celebrated "the shared humanity and brotherhood he recognized in the Sultan."

blocks.caption: 2019 picture of the saint's namesake, Pope Francis, meeting Swedish climate activist, Greta Thunberg (holding poster), at St Peter's Square Image: picture alliance / abaca

blocks.text: From mendicant friar to climate icon
But he is most widely known as an animal lover and an early figure of environmental consciousness.

"He was ahead of his time both theologically and in terms of modern natural sciences, recognizing the complexity of the cosmos and the fact that human beings are also creatures in relationship with the world around us," says Daniel Horan, author of "Francis of Assisi and the Future of Faith" (2012).
In 1979, Pope John Paul II declared Francis the patron saint of ecology, while the Argentinian Jorge Mario Bergoglio chose the saint as his papal namesake when he became Pope Francis in 2013.

blocks.caption: Copies of Pope Francis' encyclical 'Laudato Si'' or 'Praise be to you' based on St Francis' 'Canticle of the Creatures' Image: imago/ZUMA Press

blocks.text: This pope would later publish "Laudato Si'" in 2015 — based on the saint's 1225 hymn "Canticle of the Creatures," in which he addresses natural elements as "Brother Sun," "Sister Moon" and "Sister Mother Earth."

The pope's encyclical connected environmental destruction directly to human suffering, besides critiquing consumerism and the "throwaway culture," and urging humanity to undergo an "ecological conversion."

"I also believe that in a time of deep polarization and economic inequality that St Francis models another way of being in the world, one that prioritizes relationship and community over individual gain and power," says Horan.

blocks.caption: St Francis' annual feast day on October 4 is also when pets are blessed, as seen here in a church in MumbaiImage: picture alliance / Sipa USA

blocks.text: But what might Francis make of his fame today?

"It's always tricky to try and guess what St. Francis, who died 800 years ago this October, would think about anything today. Our world is so unlike his own. But we do know that in his own time he was very uncomfortable with the positive reception he and his brother friars were receiving across Europe," says Horan.
Minervini suggests that he might have been more comfortable with representations of himself as a pacifist saint.

"I suspect he would be profoundly troubled, perhaps even furious, as it is known he could get upset, by the condition of our late-capitalist, technocratic world and by the ways in which we continue to understand ourselves as separate from, and superior to, the other creatures."

articles.title: MV June Aster captain faces falsification charge over manifest entries
articles.summary: Coast Guard cites alleged discrepancies in the vessel's safety declaration and manifest.

blocks.text: September 28, 2026 | 1:25pm

This handout photo taken on September 11, 2026 and released by the Philippine coast Guard (PCG), shows an aerial shot of the ill-fated M/V June Aster with coast guard boats (L) at the stern off the shores of Coron town, Palawan province.
Philippine Coast Guard via AFP

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine Coast Guard has filed a criminal complaint against the captain of the fire-hit MV June Aster over alleged discrepancies in a safety document and the vessel's passenger manifest.

PCG spokesperson Commodore Noemie Cayabyab said a complaint for falsification of a public document was filed against Capt. Roel Sarmiento before the Department of Justice's National Prosecution Service.
The complaint involves the Master Declaration of Safe Departure, or MDSD, a sworn document submitted by the vessel's captain certifying its safety and readiness to sail.
Cayabyab said investigators found discrepancies between the MDSD and the number of people who actually boarded the vessel.

"During this incident, may anim tayong pasahero na initially na nasa ticket manifest na hindi po nakasakay sa barko. So yan po yung mga tinitingnan po natin," Cayabyab said in an interview with Super Radyo dzBB on Monday, September 28.
("During this incident, we had six passengers who were initially listed on the ticket manifest but did not board the ship. Those are among the things we are looking into.")
The PCG also found a duplicate entry for one passenger and an entry for a crew member who did not actually board the vessel.

"Pangalawa during the investigation may mga nakita rin po tayong double entry ng pangalan ng isang pasahero, at ang isa po doon ay may nakalista po na pangalan ng crew at hindi po aktwal na sumakay," Cayabyab said.
("Second, during the investigation, we also found a duplicate entry for one passenger's name, while another entry listed a crew member who did not actually board the ship.")

Under Article 172 of the Revised Penal Code, as amended by Republic Act 10951, falsification by a private individual involving a public or official document carries a penalty of prision correccional in its medium and maximum periods, or two years, four months and one day to six years, and a fine of up to P1 million.
More complaints possible
Cayabyab said the falsification complaint is only the first of possible criminal complaints arising from the investigation.
"We are now on our case build-up and we are still awaiting the forensic result," she said.
The DOJ is conducting an initial evaluation of the complaint. If prosecutors find sufficient basis, it may be docketed for preliminary investigation.

The MV June Aster caught fire off Coron, Palawan, on September 9. Authorities have confirmed 77 deaths, with 71 of the fatalities still unidentified, while eight people remain missing. Another 43 survived.
The PCG said it is still awaiting forensic findings from the Bureau of Fire Protection as it investigates the cause of the fire.

The Maritime Industry Authority is conducting a separate investigation. MARINA Region IV Director Maximo Bañares Jr. earlier said improperly stowed flammable cargo may have caused the blaze, although the agency had yet to release its final report.

articles.title: Drivers, transport operators begin 3-day strike over fuel price hikes
articles.summary: MANIBELA began a three-day transport strike on Monday, September 28, to protest rising fuel prices.

blocks.text: September 28, 2026 | 12:25pm
Passengers wait for a jeepney ride in Philcoa in Quezon City amid transport strike by Manibela on Sept. 28, 2026.
MANIBELA / Released
MANILA, Philippines — Transport group MANIBELA began a three-day transport strike on Monday, September 28, to protest rising fuel prices.

Around 6 a.m., jeepney drivers, operators and other protesters gathered along University Avenue in Quezon City before proceeding to Philcoa for a demonstration. The group said the strike will run through September 30.
MANIBELA chairperson Mar Valbuena said around 20,000 to 25,000 jeepney drivers from different routes in Metro Manila are expected to participate in the strike.
In a Facebook post, MANIBELA shared images it said showed passengers stranded due to a lack of available jeepneys.
"Pare-pareho pong hindi natin deserve ang ganitong sitwasyon lalo na at sobrang laki ng buwis ang kinukuha sa atin para nakawin lang ng iilan," the group said.
("None of us deserve this situation, especially when so much is taken from us in taxes only to be stolen by a few.")
"Pasensya na po kayo, mabigat pa rin ang presyo ng langis," it added.
("We apologize. Fuel prices remain heavy.")

During the demonstration, Valbuena confronted a person aboard a vehicle bearing a Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) sticker, accusing the person of taking photographs of the license plates of jeepneys participating in the strike.

The LTFRB had earlier warned operators that they could face sanctions if they fail to provide service as required under their franchises during the transport strikes. Acting LTFRB Chairperson Greg Pua Jr. said operators may first be issued a show-cause order and fined at least P5,000 for a first offense.

Pua said succeeding violations may lead to suspension and eventual cancellation of a franchise. The LTFRB has stressed that penalties would depend on evidence showing that an operator failed to provide the required service.
Meanwhile, transport group PISTON is set to begin its own nationwide strike on September 29 and 30, also in protest of rising fuel prices.
PISTON President Mody Floranda has estimated that 70,000 to 100,000 drivers and operators could participate.

articles.title: Cedric Lee, Deniece Cornejo release pending court clearances
articles.summary: BuCor is checking a separate sentence and awaiting court records before their release.

blocks.text: September 28, 2026 | 12:19pm
Composite image shows Cedric Lee, Deniece Cornejo and Vhong Navarro in undated photos.
The STAR / Jesse Bustos, ABS-CBN

MANILA, Philippines — Businessman Cedric Lee and model Deniece Cornejo cannot yet be released despite a Court of Appeals order reducing their sentences, as the Bureau of Corrections said it is still waiting for key court documents and must complete a final records check.

In a statement Monday, September 28, BuCor Director General Gregorio Pio Catapang Jr. said the bureau must first obtain the official entry of judgment docuemnt from the Court of Appeals and a certificate indicating no pending cases from the Taguig City Regional Trial Court.

BuCor said it is formally requesting both documents as part of its standard records validation to ensure that all legal requirements for release of the two respondents in television show host Vhong Navarro's mulling and detention have been met.
"No Entry of Judgement has been issued, therefore it is being requested before the Judicial Records Division of the said court," BuCor said.
The statement came after lawyer Ferdinand Topacio, Cornejo's former counsel, shared with reporters a copy of a Court of Appeals release order covering Cornejo and Lee.
Reduced sentences, separate conviction

Lee and Cornejo were originally sentenced by Taguig RTC Branch 153 to reclusion perpetua, or up to 40 years in prison, after being convicted of serious illegal detention for ransom involving actor-host Vhong Navarro.
The CA Special Seventeenth Division later downgraded the offense to grave coercion and reduced the penalty to a minimum of six months to a maximum of three years, six months and 21 days.
BuCor, however, said its records show that Lee and Cornejo are also serving separate sentences for another grave coercion conviction under Taguig RTC Branch 266.
That sentence, which was affirmed by the CA Ninth Division, carries the same penalty.
Because the two sentences must be served successively, BuCor said their combined prison terms range from a minimum of four years and 21 days to a maximum of seven years and 21 days.
Time credits still part of computation

BuCor's Person Deprived of Liberty Documents and Processing Division said both Lee and Cornejo have accumulated time allowances under Republic Act No. 10592, including Good Conduct Time Allowance and Time Allowance for Study, Teaching and Mentoring.
Lee has been in BuCor custody since May 3, 2024. With 460 days of GCTA, his total credited time stood at three years, 10 months and 29 days as of September 26.
BuCor calculated his presumptive minimum sentence completion date as Feb. 18, 2027, and his maximum sentence completion date as Feb. 18, 2030.
Cornejo, who has been in custody since May 2, 2024, has logged two years, four months and 24 days of actual time served, according to BuCor.
With 440 days of GCTA and 75 days of TASTM, her total credited time stood at three years, nine months and 24 days.
Her presumptive minimum sentence completion date is Dec. 23, 2026, while her maximum sentence completion date is Dec. 23, 2029.

Lee and Cornejo were imprisoned over the 2014 case filed by Navarro, who said he was attacked, restrained, threatened and held by a group that included Lee, which allegedly demanded money in exchange for his release.

articles.title: ‘The same struggles as 100 years ago’: exhibition highlights lives of Sami people in Sweden
articles.summary:
Show at Kin Museum in Kiruna marks handover of long-awaited report on abuses committed by the state against the Indigenous people

From a detailed multi-perspectival drawing of reindeer to…

blocks.text: From a detailed multi-perspectival drawing of reindeer to written accounts of belief systems and childbirth, Johan Turi’s work offers unparalleled insight into his life as a Sami person living in northern Sweden at the start of the 20th century.

In the face of racist discrimination, land disputes and the spectre of encroaching industry, Turi wanted his 1910 book Muitalus sámiid birra (An Account of the Sami) to set the record straight about the lives of Europe’s only recognised Indigenous people.
Turi is widely regarded as the first Sami author to write about Sami life in his own language, but until now his pioneering works had not been on display for almost 100 years.

blocks.caption: The artist Outi Pieski, whose art is featured in the Johan Turi exhibition at Kin. Photograph: Johan Ylitalo/Kin Museum of Contemporary Art

blocks.text: To mark the handover to the Swedish government this week of a long-awaited report by the Truth Commission for the Sami People on abuses committed by the state against the Sami, his writings, drawings, paintings and Duodji (traditional Sami handicraft) now form the centre of an exhibition at the Kin Museum of Contemporary Art in Kiruna, the area in which he used to live.
The title of the exhibition, On the Ugly and the Beautiful, draws from a quote by Turi, who died in 1936, about his belief that everything, positive and negative, has a place to be shown.
His work is on display alongside two contemporary artists, Outi Pieski and Johanna Minde.

The museum’s director, Maria Lind, said An Account of the Sami, which was published in Sami and Danish before being translated into Swedish seven years later, is “about Sami life, small and big – external and inner life”.

Turi was born in Guovdageainnu (Kautokeino), the Norwegian part of Sápmi, in 1854 but as the imposition of formal national borders began to have a bigger impact on the lives of the Sami, his family, who were reindeer herders, moved to Kiruna.

“He had dreamed about writing a book about the Sami with the purpose of making the population in Sweden understand how difficult it was for the Sami because those were difficult years,” Lind said, citing the arrival of settlers, industry, including mining, and the railway.
“He wanted the king to read his book because he felt if the king knew then things would change. Most likely the king did not read his book, but it became a success,” she added.

blocks.caption: An artwork by Outi Pieski at the Kin Museum. Photograph: Johan Ylitalo/Kin Museum

blocks.text: The problems facing Sami people today are not dissimilar to those Turi would recognise. Industry – especially the search for rare earth minerals and wind energy – is an ever-increasing threat to reindeer herding and nature. Anti-Sami rhetoric is on the rise, including from political leaders, despite the seeming progress symbolised by the truth commission and its report, which will be presented on Wednesday. Similar commissions have also been held in Norway and Finland.
But unlike in Turi’s time, there is now the escalating impact of the climate crisis, particularly visible in the Arctic and northern regions.

blocks.caption: The ládjogahpir, a traditional hat historically worn by Sami women. Photograph: Johan Ylitalo/Kin Museum

blocks.text: As the report, which is intended to form the basis for reparation and reconciliation discussions, is handed over at Mid Sweden University in Staare, the Kin Museum will put on a special tour of the works, after which there will be a reading of testimonies at the culture house next door.

Pieski, who lives on the Finnish side of Sápmi, said she grew up with Turi’s writings and drawings, in which she sees the paper as the land itself. “And then humans, animals, everything is grounded on that paper,” she said.

“It’s not a western way of seeing a landscape as a beautiful view that you look at from a distance. But the actual place where you are, physically placed, and you are an active member of this network of land.”

Her research and exploration with Eeva-Kristiina Nylander around the subject of the ládjogahpir, a traditional hat historically worn by Sami women, is also part of the exhibition. Their work has helped to bring it back into use. It has, said Pieski, become a “new symbol for decolonial feminism”.
She said that in many ways Turi’s work started the current process of truth and reconciliation by writing about life and Sami culture from his point of view.

“It’s very sad that we are kind of in the same spot still now, 100 years later,” she said. “And I know the same struggles are still existing that Johan Turi brought out with the fight for industrial land use and so on.
“No nation can exist without their own spoken or written histories. Ignoring it is a very simple colonial tool [that does] not give existence to one nation that we are here.”

articles.title: Ed Miliband to acknowledge Labour’s former stance on Palestine fell short
articles.summary:
Foreign secretary will tell party’s conference ‘we are not here to accept the status quo but to change it’

Ed Miliband will tell campaigners and party members who raised the plight of…

blocks.text: Ed Miliband will tell campaigners and party members who raised the plight of Palestinians they were right that Labour’s approach had not been enough, saying he was heeding the calls of millions of people by imposing sanctions on Israeli settlements.

The foreign secretary will tell the Labour party conference that the government will take more explicitly progressive foreign policy positions under Andy Burnham, and that the UK will be a leader among like-minded countries in a new age of diplomacy.

He will say there is a “fundamental and wider lesson from Israel and Palestine about how we have changed our approach as a party”, saying Labour will succeed “because of, not in spite of, our progressive values”.
He will talk of the start of a new and more muscular foreign policy. “We are not here to accept the status quo but to change it at home and abroad,” he will say.
The party’s conference hall was often the scene of fierce opposition to Keir Starmer’s stance on Israel and Palestine in Labour’s final year of opposition and early in government.

blocks.caption: The foreign secretary, Ed Miliband. Photograph: Wiktor Szymanowicz/Future Publishing/Getty Images

blocks.text: Since becoming foreign secretary, Miliband has announced sweeping sanctions on trade with Israeli settlements against a backdrop of increasing settler violence in the West Bank, which has resulted in 12 countries – including France and Canada – announcing they would also impose sanctions.
The Guardian understands Miliband will say in his speech that the sanctions marked a definitive change in how Labour will approach the situation in the Middle East.
“I want to say to the millions of people in this country and indeed elsewhere who have been moved and outraged by the plight of the Palestinian people: we hear you, you were right,” he will say.

“And under Andy’s leadership, we have reset our approach. We call out ethnic cleansing by the settler terrorists in the West Bank. We call out the evidence of war crimes in Gaza. We call out Israel’s illegal occupation of Palestine. And we match words with actions.
after newsletter promotion

“We will ban the import of goods from illegal settlements. We will disrupt the supply lines of British finance, British construction and British services for illegal settlements. And when it comes to the attempt to destroy the two-state solution, this party, this movement, this government, says ‘we will not let you succeed’.”

Miliband will pay tribute to those who have campaigned against the Israeli onslaught in Gaza, though his warm words are likely to raise questions about whether the government will review the proscription of Palestine Action. Police arrested a number of demonstrators outside the conference hall on Sunday.
“The bonds of solidarity between the British people and those who yearn for peace in Israel and Palestine are too strong to be broken,” Miliband will say.
“Our decision to act mobilised the international community, country after country. This is how to make change happen in today’s world. Doing what is right and galvanising others to act too.”

Miliband will say in his first speech to the party conference as foreign secretary that cooperation in imposing sanctions will be the beginning of a new bond with “likeminded countries” such as France and Canada, though it is also likely to be interpreted as being more willing to sideline the US.

Canada’s prime minister, Mark Carney, has made an explicit argument for middle powers to do more to build alliances with each other outside traditional structures, and was direct in his desire to forge closer ties with and among European countries in a speech in Brussels earlier this month.

A source close to Miliband said that would be a key theme of his time in office. “Britain’s interests are served by standing up for our values on the world stage. Our ability to build coalitions on big global issues depends on our ability to bring countries with us,” he will say.
“This Israel/Palestine reset is a sign of how we want to do business. We are going to be propositional in bringing countries with us on the issues we really care about.”

articles.title: LPG prices to fall P3 per kilo before possible P10 hike
articles.summary: he tax-driven cut may be followed by a P10-to-P15 increase in October.

blocks.text: September 28, 2026 | 11:00am
This photo taken on August 1, 2026 shows a worker cleaning a liquefied petroleum gas cylinder.
The Philippine STAR / Noel Pabalate
MANILA, Philippines — Consumers could get an LPG price cut of at least P3 per kilogram this week, only to face a much larger increase days later as global costs push higher.

Arnel Ty, president of the LPG Marketers Association, said Monday, September 28, that prices were expected to fall by at least P3 per kilogram following the government's three-month suspension of excise taxes on liquefied petroleum gas and kerosene.
But Ty also warned of a possible P10-to-P15-per-kilogram increase as early as October 3, depending on the final computation of world-market prices.
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. signed Executive Order 125 on September 25, granting the temporary excise-tax relief.
Ty said the industry learned through coordination with the Bureau of Customs that the tax-driven reduction would be implemented within the week.
Republic Gas Corp., or Regasco, will cut its LPG price by P3 per kilogram starting Wednesday, September 30.

The reduction could reach P3.36 per kilogram once the 12% value-added tax imposed on the excise tax is included, Ty said. The Department of Energy has yet to formalize the final equivalent price adjustment.

"Sa ngayon, Department of Energy na po ang magpo-formalize kung ano po ang dapat na equivalent po niyan," Ty told dzMM. ("For now, the Department of Energy will formalize the appropriate equivalent reduction.")
Relief may be short-lived
The tax relief could be quickly overwhelmed by a projected increase in LPG prices in early October.
Ty said the final adjustment would be calculated on October 1 and could take effect October 3.
He attributed the expected increase to higher world-market prices and shipping premiums amid geopolitical tensions in West Asia.
"Lubhang napakataas po ng inangat ng premium cost. It is almost $200 plus per metric ton," Ty said. ("The premium cost has risen sharply. It is almost $200-plus per metric ton.")
The excise-tax suspension will remain in effect despite the expected market-driven increase, potentially cushioning what consumers would otherwise pay.
Under the directive, the tax relief can last for up to three months. The excise tax may be restored one week after the one-month average price of Dubai crude falls below the $80-per-barrel benchmark.

articles.title: Ukraine, South Korea relations sour over North Korean POWs
articles.summary: South Korea has accused Ukraine of breaching a confidentiality agreement over the transfer of North Korean prisoners of war — and of denying the deal's existence. Seoul has demanded an apology.

image.caption: 'I do not know why the Ukrainian side broke the agreement and made the matter public, but it is very disappointing,' said Lee Jae MyungImage: Anthony Wallace/AFP

blocks.text: South Korea has demanded an official apology from Ukraine after accusing Kyiv of breaching — and then reportedly denying the existence of — a confidentiality agreement regarding the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war (POWs) to Seoul.
Last week, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced the transfer in an address to the United Nations General Assembly in New York, adding that the soldiers were "not easy to capture alive."
Hours later, South Korean President Lee Jae Myung wrote on social media: "I do not know why the Ukrainian side broke the agreement and made the matter public, but it is very disappointing."
On Sunday, the South Korean consternation was made official when Seong Ghi-hong, senior presidential secretary for public relations, demanded "an official explanation and apology."

"The presidential office expresses strong regret over Ukraine's unilateral disclosure and its subsequent false announcement that there had not been a non-disclosure agreement," Seong said in a statement.
"It is in itself a very serious matter that … seriously undermines trust between the two governments and gravely damages friendly relations between the two countries."
Seong said Seoul was "considering additional measures that may be necessary regarding this matter," but did not specify what they might be.
Why a new Russia-North Korea road bridge worries Ukraine
Ukraine: When were the North Korean soldiers captured?

The North Korean soldiers were captured by Ukrainian forces in Russia's Kursk region in January 2025 — two of around 14,000 North Korean troops deployed to the area to help halt and push back a surprise Ukrainian incursion.

Ukrainian intelligence estimates that around 3,000 North Korean troops were killed and another 1,500 injured, with the rest still stationed on Russian territory. To date, no North Korean troops are believed to have operated on Ukrainian territory itself.
Ukrainian troops reported that North Korean soldiers who were surrounded or injured on the battlefield preferred to die by suicide than surrender — and only two were captured.

Under President Lee, who has attempted to improve relations with the North, South Korea has appeared hesitant to take custody of the pair. But, under Article 3 of the South Korean constitution, North Koreans are still considered citizens of the South and are permitted to live in the South.
South Korea is an ally of Ukraine, albeit one which has so far only provided non-lethal aid. But Kyiv has been pressing Seoul to provide advanced air defense systems.
Last month, President Zelenskyy claimed that up to 50,000 more North Korean troops could be deployed to Russia.

articles.title: LIVE UPDATES: Impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte
articles.summary: Bookmark this page for Rappler's comprehensive coverage of Vice President Sara Duterte's impeachment trial at the Senate

blocks.text: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte — the first Philippine public official to be impeached twice by the House of Representatives — began at 2 pm on Monday, July 6.

There are four articles of impeachment against Duterte involving alleged misuse of confidential funds, unexplained wealth, bribery of Department of Education officials, and grave threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his family.

Only 21 out of 24 senator-judges are physically present. Senator Bato dela Rosa remains in hiding as he faces an International Criminal Court arrest warrant over Rodrigo Duterte’s drug war, Senator Jinggoy Estrada has been detained and suspended in connection with a plunder case, and Senator Rodante Marcoleta surrendered to authorities as he also faces a plunder case.
On this page, we bring you the latest updates, analyses, videos, and photos as the trial of the Vice President unfolds.

blocks.text: LATEST UPDATES
18 minutes ago
Baste Duterte yet to say if he would appear at impeachment trial today
The Senate impeachment court has subpoenaed Davao City Mayor Baste Duterte from Monday, September 28, to Wednesday, September 30, 2026.
However, Senate Sergeant-at-Arms Alfred Corpuz says Duterte did not inform the court if he would appear at the trial on Monday.
Corpuz also says there will be no changes in the security protocols in the Senate.
Duterte was issued with a subpoena to testify in the impeachment trial of his older sister, Vice President Sara Duterte.

Rappler Recap: Senate lowers Sara Duterte conviction threshold; minority senators skip vote

The Senate impeachment court on Wednesday, September 23, votes 13-1 to lower the voting threshold for convicting Vice President Sara Duterte, with six senator-judges not participating in the vote. The court says the new computation will exclude members legally or factually unable to participate in the trial.

blocks.text: Sep 24, 2026 8:30 AM PHT
Rappler Recap: How lower conviction threshold changes the math in Sara Duterte’s trial

The Senate impeachment court on Wednesday, September 23, lowers the voting threshold for conviction in Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial, changing the number of votes needed based on the senator-judges eligible to participate in the proceedings.
Rappler multimedia reporter Dwight de Leon explains how the ruling could affect the prosecution and defense, the possible new conviction threshold, and how both sides reacted to the decision.

blocks.caption: LIVE UPDATES: Impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte

blocks.text: Sep 23, 2026 9:07 PM PHT
Litigator counters Poa’s argument against lowering voting threshold

“Moving the threshold in terms of impeachment because it serves accountability does not have to mean moving the threshold elsewhere — bogeyman ‘yun,” litigator and Free Legal Assistance member Raffy Aquino said in a Rappler panel discussion during Day 29 of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial on Wednesday, September 23.

The comment was made following defense lawyer Michael Poa’s argument that lowering the voting threshold for impeachment could have consequences on other constitutional provisions, such as revoking or extending martial law, expulsion of a member of the Senate, or amending the Constitution itself. – Rhen Peñada
Sep 23, 2026 8:54 PM PHT
A Villar split: Why is Mark Villar breaking ranks with sister Camille?
Two roads diverged in the Senate on Wednesday, September 23 — and the Villar siblings took different ones.

Senator-judge Mark Villar broke ranks with his sister, Senator-judge Camille Villar, and the Senate minority bloc in a surprise vote on two key motions during the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.
Sep 23, 2026 7:36 PM PHT
Change in voting threshold not yet a ‘justiciable controversy’

Litigator and Free Legal Assistance Group member Raffy Aquino stressed on Wednesday, September 23, that the change in the voting threshold for the impeachment trial does not yet present a “justiciable controversy” that could be reviewed by the Supreme Court (SC).
“There is no injury yet. The Vice President still remains as vice president. And there is no vote yet on the conviction or acquittal,” he explained.
Aquino added that while the SC’s power of judicial review has been expanded to preserve its checking function, it remains limited and requires an actual controversy and grave abuse of discretion.
He added that if the previous threshold of 16 votes is still met, “then there is no controversy” since the conviction would stand.

Based on his experience as an “occasional constitutional litigator,” Aquino said the SC “does not easily lend itself to obstructions,” emphasizing that there must first be an actual controversy before the Court could intervene. – Rena Eñano
Sep 23, 2026 6:14 PM PHT
Why did Mark Villar vote differently from sister Camille?

Following the Senate impeachment court vote on the conviction voting threshold, litigator Raffy Aquino says on Wednesday, September 23, that the Villar siblings Mark and Camille showed one of two things: they either “demonstrated how it is to vote according to one’s conscience,” or it was a strategy to have a foot on either side of the door.

Lawyer Paolo Panelo, spokesperson of Vice President Sara Duterte, says the Senate ruling lowering the cinviction vote threshold was “unfavorable” to the public.

articles.title: 'We will not be intimidated': Tk'emlúps te Secwépemc chief after reported white nationalist gathering
articles.summary: B.C. politicians and leaders are denouncing an apparent gathering of white nationalists on the Tk'emlúps te Secwépemc reserve near Kamloops, B.C. Kúkpi7 Rosanne Casimir says the nation received…

image.caption: Rosanne Casimir, Chief of the Tk'emlúps te Secwépemc, says this incident will not deter the community from 'gathering, reflecting, or honoring our survivors and the children who returned home.' (Ben Nelms/CBC)

blocks.text: British Columbia

B.C. politicians and leaders are denouncing an apparent gathering of white nationalists on the Tk'emlúps te Secwépemc reserve near Kamloops, B.C. Kúkpi7 Rosanne Casimir says the nation received reports Sunday morning of roughly 30 masked men on the reserve.
B.C. politicians and leaders condemn reported gathering, calling it 'disgraceful' and 'hateful'
B.C. politicians and leaders are denouncing an apparent gathering of white nationalists on the Tk'emlúps te Secwépemc reserve, just east of Kamloops.

Tk'emlúps te Secwépemc Kúkpi7 Rosanne Casimir says the nation received reports Sunday morning of a gathering of roughly 30 men, donning white face masks and black caps, standing together around the reserve while hoisting flags over their shoulders.

In a press release, Casimir said "individuals associated with Second Sons Canada, a group linked to white supremacist and white nationalist ideology, have been seen and documented within our community."
"White supremacy will not instill fear in generations of survivors and intergenerational survivors who have already carried fear for far too long," said Casimir in the release.

Images circulating on social media appear to show logos on flags and clothing affiliated with Second Sons Canada. However, CBC News has not been able to independently verify the identities of the individuals or their group affiliations.
Casimir told CBC News that the reserve's security told the men they were not permitted to gather and asked them to leave. However, they did not leave until RCMP were called and arrived at the scene.

items: Leaders in B.C. release joint statement condemning anti-Indigenous racism

blocks.text: CBC News reached out to the RCMP but did not hear back before publication.

Speaking at the Vancouver International Airport Sunday afternoon, NDP Leader David Eby said there has been a rise "in this kind of white nationalist behaviour" in B.C., adding that more needs to be done "to fight it."

"This is just disgraceful, disgusting behaviour. It's very clear that these people were trying to intimidate, make people feel fearful," said the premier, adding that the men in face masks would face severe retribution if their identities were known.

"The white nationalist gathering on Tk'emlúps te Secwépemc land this morning was hateful and meant to intimidate. It has no place in British Columbia," said Lorne Doerkson, interim leader of the B.C. Conservative Party, in a post to social media.
He added that the "B.C. Conservatives condemn it completely."

items: Anti-Indigenous racism increasing around Powell River, say Tla'amin Nation citizens

blocks.text: CentreBC Leader Elenore Sturko, in a post on social media, called the gathering "abhorrent."

"Hate and discrimination of any kind are unwelcome in British Columbia and on behalf of all members of Centre BC, I condemn this behaviour and stand in solidarity with the Tkʼemlúps First Nation," she said.
Plans for the nation's events for Truth and Reconciliation Day on Sept. 30, Casimir said, will go ahead.
"We will not be intimidated," said Casimir.
"This is not going to deter us from gathering, reflecting, or honouring our survivors and the children who returned home," she said.
But this incident, Casimir said, is an example of a broader problem.
"Everyone should always be concerned because there's so much racism and discrimination out there."
She said Tk'emlúps te Secwépemc will keep its community members informed if there are further safety concerns.
CBC News reached out to Second Sons Canada but did not hear back before publication.
A national 24-hour Indian Residential School Crisis Line is available at 1-866-925-4419 for emotional and crisis referral services for survivors and those affected.
Mental health counselling and crisis support are also available 24 hours a day, seven days a week through the Hope for Wellness hotline at 1-855-242-3310 or by online chat.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Arden McLeod, from Vancouver, is an associate producer with CBC News. He has a passion for community storytelling, local news, and reflecting the values of B.C. He graduated from the British Columbia Institute of Technology's broadcast and online journalism program. You can reach him at Arden.McLeod@cbc.ca.
With files from Tara Copeland

articles.title: France’s far-right National Rally surges in Senate elections
articles.summary:
Marine Le Pen hails ‘historic victory’ as her party and allies win enough seats to form caucus just months ahead of presidential poll

France’s far-right National Rally (RN) party and its…

blocks.text: France’s far-right National Rally (RN) party and its allies have secured a record 14 seats in the rightwing-dominated Senate in elections, effectively quadrupling its number in the 348-seat chamber just months before a presidential poll.
RN presidential candidate Marine Le Pen called the results an “historic victory” after they were announced on Sunday. “The results ‌have exceeded our expectations,” she said.
It was the first time the ⁠party had cleared the 10-seat threshold to be able to form a Senate caucus.
Local elected officials vote for new senators for half the upper chamber every three years, each to serve a six-year term.
The far-right party entered the Senate for the first time with two seats in 2014, when it was known as the National Front, and won three seats in 2023.
Le Pen is considering her best chance yet at power in elections scheduled for a first round in April next year when the centrist president, Emmanuel Macron, steps down.
“This is a historic victory, and a major milestone with the formation for the first time of a group in the Senate,” she said on X.
Nine RN senators were elected on Sunday, according to an AFP tally of results, on top of the three who won seats in 2023.
A further two were elected from RN ally Eric Ciotti’s Union of the Right for the Republic (UDR) party.
RN’s president, Jordan Bardella, said the party’s senators would form a group with UDR allies.

blocks.caption: RN president Jordan Bardella (C) poses with supporters in La Seyne-sur-Mer, southern France, on Sunday as the far right won a record 14 seats in Senate elections. Photograph: Thibaud Moritz/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Ciotti quit the rightwing Republicans (LR) party in 2024 after calling for an alliance with the far right.
The upper chamber’s LR president of more than a decade, Gerard Larcher, 77, is expected to be re-elected next week.
The right, centre and leftwing Socialists looked set to remain the three major forces in the upper house, according to initial results.
The hard-left France Unbowed party won a seat for the first time.
Le Pen’s anti-immigration party emerged as the single largest party in the lower-house National Assembly after Macron called snap polls in 2024, although it fell well short of a majority.
With Reuters

articles.title: Beau Lamarre-Condon told friend if he killed anyone he’d dump belongings in bin and take bodies to bushland, court hears
articles.summary: Former police officer has pleaded not guilty to murdering Jesse Baird and Luke Davies in early 2024 – nine months after discussion with friend Georgia Cook

blocks.text: A Sydney police officer told a friend he would hide the bodies of anyone he killed in bushland and put their belongings in a dumpster, months before allegedly murdering Jesse Baird and Luke Davies, a court has been told.
Beau Lamarre-Condon, 31, has been accused of fatally shooting the couple with a police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024.
He has pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one charge of aggravated break and enter.
At his double murder trial on Monday, Georgia Cook, a close friend of Lamarre-Condon, told the NSW supreme court about a dinner in May 2023.
The brief relationship between Baird and Lamarre-Condon had ended when the accused asked her what she would do if he told her he’d killed someone, Cook told the jury.
He then asked what she would do if she killed someone and what she would do with their bodies, the court heard. Cook responded she had no idea.

She said on Monday that Lamarre-Condon replied: “After I’d killed them I would take their stuff, I would put it in a dumpster, and I would take their bodies in bushland where nobody would ever find them.”
Asked about her response, Cook said the situation in 2023 felt “very surreal”.
“I didn’t know whether to believe anything I’d heard, or whether it was true,” she told the jury.
“Hearing a person of power in the police force [say that] – it felt like I didn’t have anywhere to go and I was really scared by what I had heard.”
after newsletter promotion

After Lamarre-Condon allegedly shot Baird and Davies in February 2024, he dumped Baird’s bloodied belongings and furniture into a skip bin in Cronulla, the prosecution said during its opening statement last week.
The two bodies were found on the fence line of a Greek orthodox monastery in remote bushland in Bungonia – about 200km from Paddington.

Cook on Friday told the court that Lamarre-Condon told her he had been watching Baird from outside his home. The crown alleged in its opening that the police officeer began planning to murder Baird in early 2024.
The defence team has claimed he was acting in self-defence after he disguised himself as an UberEats rider and entered Baird’s home on the day of the shootings.
The trial before justice Natalie Adams continues.

articles.title: Rains forecast over Visayas, parts of Mindanao as ITCZ prevails
articles.summary: The ITCZ is forecast to bring scattered rains and thunderstorms to the Visayas, Palawan and parts of Mindanao on Monday.

blocks.text: September 28, 2026 | 8:59am
Satellite-based rendering shows the relative location of cyclone Surigae (formerly 'Queenie) north of the Philippines as of 8:50 a.m. on Monday, Sept. 28, 2026.
JMA

MANILA, Philippines — The intertropical convergence zone is forecast to bring scattered rains and thunderstorms over the Visayas, Palawan and parts of Mindanao on Monday, September 28, with possible flash floods or landslides during moderate to at times heavy rains.
In its 4 a.m. weather forecast, PAGASA said the ITCZ is affecting Palawan, the Visayas and Mindanao.
The ICTZ is a weather system of converging winds that force air upward, creating heavy clouds, thunderstorms and rainfall.
Cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms are forecast over the Visayas, Zamboanga Peninsula, Northern Mindanao, Caraga, Palawan and Lanao del Sur.
PAGASA warned that moderate to at times heavy rains in these areas could trigger flash floods or landslides.
The rest of Mindanao is forecast to have partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rain showers or thunderstorms due to the ITCZ. Flash floods or landslides may occur during severe thunderstorms.
Metro Manila and the rest of Luzon, meanwhile, may experience partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rain showers or thunderstorms caused by localized thunderstorms.
PAGASA also warned of possible flash floods or landslides during severe thunderstorms in these areas.
Typhoon remains outside PAR
Typhoon Surigae, formerly known as Queenie while inside the Philippine area of responsibility, remained outside PAR early Monday.
As of 3 a.m., the typhoon was located 1,055 kilometers northeast of extreme northern Luzon.
Surigae was packing maximum sustained winds of 175 kilometers per hour near the center, with gusts of up to 215 kph. It was moving east-northeastward at 15 kph.
PAGASA said winds across Luzon will be light to moderate and variable, with slight to moderate coastal waters ranging from 0.6 to 1.5 meters.
The Visayas and Mindanao will likewise have light to moderate winds, blowing from the southeast to southwest, with coastal waters of 0.6 to 1.5 meters.

articles.title: Watch: Shipwreck uncovered on Nantucket island during nor'easter storm
articles.summary: The so-called nor'easter storm has washed up what may be a shipwreck from the 19th century in Massachusetts, local media says.

blocks.text: A powerful nor'easter storm has washed up what may be a shipwreck from the 19th century in Massachusetts, local media said.
The wreckage discovered on a beach on Sunday is believed to be part of the "Warren Sawyer" – which ran aground near Nantucket in 1884, according to the Nantucket Current.
Fragments of the wooden ship were also discovered in 2022 and 2023.
Heavy rainfall and dangerous coastal flooding have hit parts of north-eastern US, with more than 160,000 households experiencing power cuts.

articles.title: Trump asked Xi Jinping if China would like to buy US weapons, American ambassador says
articles.summary:
David Perdue’s remarks come after a Taiwanese minister spoke of the ‘severe’ military threat posed by Beijing to the self-ruled island

Donald Trump offered to sell weapons to China while…

blocks.text: Donald Trump offered to sell weapons to China while hosting its leader, Xi Jinping, last week, the US ambassador to China said on Sunday.
David Perdue told Fox News on Sunday: “President Trump continues to say, hey, we sell arms to other people around the world. He actually asked President Xi, would he like to buy some at one point.”

The extraordinary claim came during an interview about US policy on Taiwan, which has been waiting for months for Trump to approve a new arms sales ⁠package worth $14bn, after a record multi-billion dollar deal was unveiled in December last year.

Trump’s level of commitment to protecting Taiwan has previously been questioned. At a meeting with Xi in Beijing in May, ⁠Trump said he was keeping the $14bn Taiwan arms sales package in abeyance, describing it as a “very good negotiating chip” in dealings with China.

Washington has long maintained a strategically ambiguous stance on whether it would defend Taiwan in the event of an invasion. But under the decades-old Taiwan Relations Act, it is required to provide Taipei with sufficient military equipment to defend itself.

Beijing has repeatedly said it “resolutely opposes” Washington’s arms sales to the island democracy, which it regards as a breakaway province, despite never having ruled it, and has not renounced the use of force to take. During their Washington meeting last week, Xi urged Trump to oppose “Taiwan independence,” according to a readout from the official Chinese news agency Xinhua.

After Purdue’s interview, the White House told the New York Times that the US had no plans to sell arms to China, while the state department said: “US law prohibits arms sales to China and there is no offer or plan to sell arms to China.”
Before the interview, Taiwanese deputy foreign minister Chen Ming-chi spoke of the severe military threat China posed.

“Taiwan faces a severe situation in the Taiwan strait. Even though China’s economy is declining, it continues investing more resources into building military capacity. Under ‌this context, the US very much understands our defence needs,” he told reporters in Taipei.
Trump ​has not mentioned the sale ‌since last week’s summit, saying ‌only on Saturday that Xi understands his position on Taiwan.
Perdue himself told CNBC ​on Friday that there had been ​no change in Taiwan policy by Trump, including on arms ​sales.
With Reuters

articles.title: Northeast U.S. pummelled by wind and floods from deadly nor'easter
articles.summary: Residents of coastal communities in the U.S. northeast slogged through floodwaters for a second day as a powerful nor'easter pummelled the shoreline Sunday, knocking out power to tens of thousands of…

image.caption: A pedestrian and a car navigate a street as a wave crashes into a seawall in Hampton, N.H., on Sunday. (C.J. Gunther/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New

Residents of coastal communities in the U.S. northeast slogged through floodwaters for a second day as a powerful nor'easter pummelled the shoreline Sunday, knocking out power to tens of thousands of homes.
New York City housing authority worker died after falling from tree
Tidal surges swamped low-lying neighbourhoods in New Jersey while wind gusts toppled trees on New York's Long Island, damaging homes and bringing down utility poles.

In the New Jersey beach town of Sea Bright, each high tide brought a new round of flooding. "It's not like a one-time occurrence," said Caroline Virenius, whose garage filled with about a foot of water. "It's getting wet again and again."

The slow-moving storm, which killed a New York City housing authority worker when a tree fell Saturday, was expected to linger through Sunday with heavy rain, strong winds and dangerous surf all the way to New England.

Extreme amounts of rain — more than 10 centimetres since Friday in some spots in New Jersey — combined with a surging ocean led to flooding amounts not seen for close to a decade in places used to dealing with high water, residents said.
Flights, utilities affected

The nor'easter triggered memories of Superstorm Sandy, which left behind over $60 billion US in damage across the eastern U.S. in 2012. While this storm's impact has been nowhere near that, it could be the first of several along the East Coast this fall because of an El Niño climate pattern that's disrupting this year's weather.
Images of waves crashing into sea walls and onto beaches raised concerns about coastal erosion.

items: Powerful storm causes widespread flooding, outages in northeast U.S.

blocks.text: Well over 100,000 customers were without power across the Northeast and mid-Atlantic at times on Sunday, according to PowerOutage.us. The most widespread outages were in counties along the coast from New Jersey to Connecticut.

Numerous flights were cancelled or delayed up and down the coast. More than 250 flights had been cancelled at Boston Logan International Airport by late Sunday morning as wind gusts reached 64 km/h, according to the Massachusetts Port Authority.
Flooding concern
The worst of the remaining rainfall was expected Sunday from northern New Jersey into southern New England.
While the storm was gradually weakening, tidal flooding would stay through high-tide cycles Sunday night, said Bob Oravec, a lead forecaster with the National Weather Service in College Park, Md.

items: Some TV meteorologists want to talk about climate change. Not everyone wants to hear it

blocks.text: In New York City, water a few inches deep filled streets in the Howard Beach neighbourhood but didn't deter residents from venturing out for coffee Sunday morning.
Carole Ann Palmer, who owns Jingles Bait and Tackle in North Beach Haven, N.J., said this was the worst flooding she's seen in 10 years.
"Yesterday, I was like, oh my God, it just keeps getting higher and higher," said Palmer, who lives above the store.
The front step was swept away in the storm and she saw neighbours kayaking through the streets on Saturday.

items: Hawaii readies for arrival of Hurricane Nolo amid risks of catastrophic flooding

blocks.text: Her biggest problem on Sunday was taking her two puppies outside to relieve themselves. She had to put on waders and carry them to dry land.
"I take one at the time, carry them across the street so they can do their business and then come back, dry them off and then do the other one. It's a workout," Palmer said.
N.J. community better prepared after Sandy
Bernard Dowd waded through tidal water Sunday to get to his Sea Bright home, a day after he got back from work to find his basement "filled up like a swimming pool."

But he said the situation around his neighbourhood likely would have been much worse if it weren't for new rules requiring homeowners to raise the height of their homes in the wake of Sandy, which devastated the community.

items: The weatherman who spoke the truth – and paid the price

blocks.text: He also noticed that many around the community had lined their home and businesses with sandbags — something he wishes he would have done.
"I'm always thinking they are hyping the storm," he said.

articles.title: Israel strips Dutch diplomats of status in West Bank
articles.summary: The move by the Israeli Foreign Ministry is a response to Dutch sanctions targeting goods from illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank. The Dutch Foreign Ministry is yet to comment.

image.caption: 'Israel will not ignore measures intended to harm it,' Foreign Minister Gideon Saar wrote on social mediaImage: Sebastian Christoph Gollnow/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: The Israeli government said on Sunday that it was revoking the diplomatic status of Dutch diplomats representing The Netherlands at the Palestinian Authority in Ramallah, the administrative capital of the Palestinian Territories.
Israeli ​Foreign Minister Gideon Saar said the move was a response to Dutch sanctions targeting illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.
"Israel will not ignore measures intended to harm it," Saar wrote on social media.
He ordered Dutch diplomats operating in Ramallah to ​return their Israeli-issued diplomatic documentation within seven days.
"After this period, the diplomatic privileges and immunities granted to them by the State of Israel will expire," he added.
Israeli settlement trade ban widens across Europe
Dutch ban on settlement goods: what does it entail?
Dutch authorities announced earlier this month that they would begin enforcing a ban on settlement goods.

The ban, which applies to personal baggage as well as commercial shipments, came into force on September 22 and, in recent days, Dutch and Israeli media have reported that passengers arriving at Amsterdam's Schiphol airport from Israel had their luggage searched for banned goods.

Earlier in September, Israel also ordered the closure of ⁠the British Consulate ⁠in East Jerusalem, the United Kingdom's representative to the Palestinian Authority, after London announced similar sanctions banning the import of goods from illegal settlements.
"Any country that acts in a hostile and unilateral manner against Israel will lose influence and relevance in the region," said Saar.
France and Canada have also announced a ban on goods from settlements, but Israel has not yet taken any action against ​those two countries.
In August, Israel also banned Dutch diplomats from a Israeli-based, US-led coordination center for Gaza over what the foreign minister described as "anti-Israel measures."
